objects.description: Platform-dependent signed size type used by OpenSSL public headers. It is defined as a typedef to an appropriate underlying integer type depending on the target platform and configuration (e.g., __int64 on Win64, int on Win32, ssize_t on POSIX, INTN on UEFI).
8-bit signed integer type for UEFI builds where standard inttypes/stdint headers are unavailable.
8-bit unsigned integer type for UEFI builds where standard inttypes/stdint headers are unavailable.
16-bit signed integer type for UEFI builds.
16-bit unsigned integer type for UEFI builds.
32-bit signed integer type for UEFI builds.
32-bit unsigned integer type for UEFI builds.
64-bit signed integer type for UEFI builds.
64-bit unsigned integer type for UEFI builds.
Unsigned integer type capable of holding a pointer for UEFI builds.
8-bit signed integer type used on older MSVC that lack stdint/inttypes. Note: multiple conditional typedefs exist; only one applies per build configuration.
8-bit unsigned integer type for older MSVC configurations.
16-bit signed integer type for older MSVC configurations.
16-bit unsigned integer type for older MSVC configurations.
32-bit signed integer type for older MSVC configurations.
32-bit unsigned integer type for older MSVC configurations.
64-bit signed integer type for older MSVC configurations.
64-bit unsigned integer type for older MSVC configurations.
Maximum-width signed integer type alias used by OpenSSL when C99 intmax_t is available; otherwise falls back to 64-bit signed integer.
Maximum-width unsigned integer type alias used by OpenSSL when C99 uintmax_t is available; otherwise falls back to 64-bit unsigned integer.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains include guards, a pragma once, and includes of other headers. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document from this file.
Deprecated placeholder type for dynamic locks from pre-1.1.0 OpenSSL. No longer used; retained for source compatibility only. Structure carries no usable fields.
Opaque read/write lock handle used by OpenSSL threading/atomics utilities. Created and freed via CRYPTO_THREAD_* APIs in this header.

Holds per-object application-defined extra data (ex_data) for various OpenSSL object classes. Contains a library context pointer and a stack of void pointers. Managed via CRYPTO_new_ex_data/CRYPTO_dup_ex_data/CRYPTO_free_ex_data and CRYPTO_set/get_ex_data.
Deprecated thread identifier wrapper (pre-1.1.0). No longer used by OpenSSL; kept for source compatibility. Contains no meaningful fields.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*CRYPTO_malloc_fn)(size_t num, const char *file, int line);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom malloc hooks receiving size and allocation site. Install via CRYPTO_set_mem_functions.

objects.definition:
typedef void *(*CRYPTO_realloc_fn)(void *addr, size_t num, const char *file,
    int line);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom realloc hooks receiving old pointer, new size, and allocation site. Install via CRYPTO_set_mem_functions.

objects.definition: typedef void (*CRYPTO_free_fn)(void *addr, const char *file, int line);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom free hooks receiving pointer and free site. Install via CRYPTO_set_mem_functions.

Thread-local storage key type used by OpenSSL portable threading abstraction in the fallback configuration (when platform-specific typedefs are not active). Managed via CRYPTO_THREAD_init_local/get_local/set_local/cleanup_local.
Thread identifier type used by OpenSSL portable threading abstraction in the fallback configuration (when platform-specific typedefs are not active). Obtain via CRYPTO_THREAD_get_current_id.

One-time initialization control variable for OpenSSL portable threading abstraction in the fallback configuration (when platform-specific typedefs are not active). Use with CRYPTO_THREAD_run_once; initialize with CRYPTO_ONCE_STATIC_INIT.

Per-thread OpenSSL error queue state. Holds circular buffers of recent error records (codes, data, file/line/function) plus mark/flag arrays and indices. Constructed and managed internally by the ERR subsystem; callers may retrieve or manipulate the current thread’s state via provided APIs. Lifetime is managed by OpenSSL; do not free unless using the provided OSSL_ERR_STATE_* APIs.
Mapping entry from an error code to its human-readable string. Used when loading or unloading error string tables for libraries.

Opaque or forward-declared parameter descriptor type used throughout the OpenSSL provider/core parameter passing API. This header references OSSL_PARAM extensively but does not define it; it is expected to be defined in included headers (e.g., <openssl/core.h>). Purpose: represent a single typed parameter (name, data type, buffer pointer, size, return size/modified flag). Details of its fields are unknown from this header alone.
OpenSSL big integer type used with OSSL_PARAM BN accessors. It is only referenced here; its definition is not present in this header (it comes from <openssl/bn.h>).
Parameter record used with TLS1.1 multiblock control operations for ciphers. Holds pointers to output and input buffers, total input length, and interleave factor for multiblock processing.
Small helper struct bundling an EVP_CIPHER algorithm pointer with a fixed-size IV buffer suitable for use in envelope/cipher parameter handling.
Algorithm identifier structure pairing an ASN.1 object identifier with optional parameters, used across X.509/PKCS structures to denote signature and key algorithms.
Stack container holding X509_ALGOR elements.
Validity period with notBefore and notAfter times for certificates.
Opaque PKCS#7/PKCS#8 digest info wrapper (DigestInfo/PKCS#8 EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo). Only forward-declared here; full layout not present.
Opaque single RDN attribute (type/value) inside an X509_NAME. Layout not in this header.
Opaque X.509 v3 extension. Creation helpers provided to set object, criticality and data.
Stack of X509_EXTENSION entries.
Opaque attribute (type/value set) used with requests and PKCS#8 attributes.
Opaque internal container for X.509 certificate request TBSCertRequest fields.
Opaque X.509 certificate signing request (CSR).
Opaque auxiliary certificate info (trust/reject, alias, keyid) accompanying a certificate.
Opaque TBSCertificate info component of an X.509 certificate.
Opaque TBSCRL info component of a certificate revocation list.
Legacy wrapper for encrypted/decrypted private key material with associated algorithm and cipher info. Mostly for compatibility and PEM parsing.
Bundle used by PEM routines to carry a cert, CRL, private key and optional encrypted blob from a single input.
Netscape Signed Public Key and Challenge (SPKAC) body holding a public key and challenge string.
Netscape SPKI structure encapsulating an SPKAC and its signature algorithm and signature.
Netscape certificate sequence containing an object type and a stack of certificates.
Parameters for legacy PKCS#5 v1.5 PBE (salt and iteration count).
PKCS#5 v2.0 PBE2 parameters: key derivation function and encryption scheme algorithms.
PBKDF2 parameters including salt, iteration count, optional key length, and PRF algorithm.
PBMAC1 parameters pairing a KDF and a MAC scheme algorithms.
scrypt KDF parameters: salt and cost (N), block size (r), parallelization (p), and output key length. Only available when scrypt is enabled.
Opaque method table for customizing X509_CRL behavior (init, free, lookup, verify). Only referenced via API; not defined here.
Descriptor for an X.509 v3 extension: identifies the NID, flags, ASN.1 item or conversion callbacks between encodings, text and CONF values. Used to register/handle custom extensions.
Context passed to extension builders: carries issuer/subject certs or req, CRL, config DB and flags for extension processing.
Set of callbacks to access configuration data (strings/sections) for extension parsing.
Alias typedef for BIT_STRING_BITNAME used to label bit names in bit strings. No extra semantics beyond aliasing.
X.509 BasicConstraints extension structure: indicates CA capability and optional path length constraint.
OpenSSL-specific basic attribute constraints: similar to BasicConstraints but with 'authority' field naming.
PrivateKeyUsagePeriod extension: notBefore/notAfter times for key usage validity.
GeneralName otherName choice: OID/type and ASN.1 value.
EDI party name structure for GeneralName choice.
Represents a GeneralName per RFC 5280 with multiple possible name forms selected by type.
AuthorityInfoAccess/SubjectInfoAccess entry: access method OID and access location GeneralName.
Sequence of ACCESS_DESCRIPTION for AIA/SIA extensions.
Sequence of key purpose OIDs for Extended Key Usage.
RFC 7633 TLS Feature extension: sequence of feature integers.
Sequence of GENERAL_NAME entries (e.g., SubjectAltName, IssuerAltName).
CRL distribution point name: either fullName (GENERAL_NAMES) or relative name with associated full DN.
CRL distribution point entry: optional name, reasons bitstring, optional CRL issuer and cached reason mask.
Sequence of DIST_POINT structures for CRL Distribution Points extension.
AuthorityKeyIdentifier extension: key identifier, authority issuer names and serial.
Strong Extranet ID pair: zone (integer) and user (octet string).
Strong Extranet (SXNET) extension container: version and list of SXNETID entries.
Holds metadata strings about issuer signing tools (non-standard extension).
Policy qualifier NoticeReference: organization and notice numbers.
Policy qualifier UserNotice: optional notice reference and explicit text.
Policy qualifier info: qualifier id and associated data (CPS URI, UserNotice or other).
Certificate policy information: policy OID and optional qualifiers.
Sequence of POLICYINFO structures used in the certificatePolicies extension.
Maps issuer domain policy OID to subject domain policy OID (PolicyMappings extension). POLICY_MAPPINGS is a SEQUENCE OF these.
Name constraints subtree: base GeneralName with optional min/max exclusions.
NameConstraints extension: permitted and excluded name subtrees.
PolicyConstraints extension fields for requiring explicit policy and inhibiting policy mapping.
Proxy policy descriptor: language OID and optional policy data.
ProxyCertInfo extension: optional path length and proxy policy.
IssuingDistributionPoint extension: constraints on CRL scope and usage.
Represents an application-defined certificate purpose with associated check function and metadata.
RFC3779 AS number range with inclusive min/max.
Choice of a single AS number or a range for RFC3779 AS identifiers.
Choice indicating AS identifiers are inherited or explicitly listed (RFC3779).
Top-level RFC3779 ASIdentifiers extension: autonomous system numbers and routing domain identifiers.
Represents an inclusive IP address range as bit strings (RFC3779).
Choice of IP address prefix or address range entry (RFC3779).
Indicates IP resources are inherited or explicitly specified via addresses/ranges (RFC3779).
One address family entry for IP resources: AFI/SAFI and associated choice of resources.
Sequence of IPAddressFamily structures for RFC3779 IP Resources extension.
Opaque forward typedef; full structure definition is not present in this header. Details unknown.
Opaque forward typedef for profession information used in Admission Syntax. Full fields not defined here.
Opaque forward typedef for an Admissions entry within Admission Syntax. Definition not included here.
Opaque forward typedef for AdmissionSyntax extension container. Definition not included here.
Structure identifying a role-specific certificate via names, issuer, serial and optional locator.
Sequence of OSSL_ROLE_SPEC_CERT_ID entries.
AlgorithmIdentifier plus hash value container used by various custom info syntaxes.
Pointer-type variant for OSSL_INFO_SYNTAX: references a named object and its hash.
Information syntax used in privilege policy descriptors: either embedded content or a pointer (name+hash).
Associates a privilege policy OID with an information syntax describing it.
Describes an attribute: identifier OID, syntax, display name/description and optional policy domination rule.
Absolute time window with start and end generalized times.
Represents a time of day (hour, minute, second).
A time band within a day delimited by start and end times.
Represents named days either by integer list or bitset.
Specifies the Nth occurrence (first..fifth) of named days within a period.
Day selection within a schedule: integer set, bitset, or by Nth weekday specification.
Week selection: all, integer list, or bitset of weeks.
Month selection: all, integer list, or bitset of months.
Periodic time specification combining times of day, day/week/month selections and years.
Top-level time type: absolute window or periodic schedules.
Comprehensive time specification including time definition, negation flag and timezone.
Attribute Type and Value pair used in attribute mapping constructs.
Maps a local attribute OID to a remote attribute OID.
Maps a local attribute type+value to a remote type+value.
Choice item for attribute mapping: either type mapping or type+value mapping. OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPINGS is a SEQUENCE OF these.
Sequence of OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPING entries.
Choice describing an allowed attribute either by OID type or a full X509_ATTRIBUTE type+values.
Container specifying allowed attributes and an optional holder domain name.
Sequence of allowed attribute items defining policy constraints.
Attribute Authority distribution point entry similar to CRL DP with AA-specific flags.
Sequence of X509_ATTRIBUTE used in custom syntaxes; typedef only.
Sequence of USERNOTICE structures; typedef only.

Callback function type used by PEM read/write routines to obtain a passphrase. It is referenced throughout this header but its actual typedef is not defined here (it is defined elsewhere in OpenSSL headers). Details such as signature and semantics are therefore unknown in this header context.
Typedef alias to a pointer to struct ssl_st used to silence compiler warnings for callback prototypes. It names the pointer type ssl_crock_st, but does not define struct ssl_st here.
Opaque alias to struct tls_session_ticket_ext_st. Represents TLS session ticket extension data. The struct itself is not defined in this header.
Opaque method descriptor for SSL/TLS protocol implementations (client/server, version families). Not defined here; constructed via functions like TLS_method().

Opaque descriptor for a single SSL/TLS cipher/ciphersuite. Structure not defined here; accessed via various SSL_CIPHER_get_* APIs. Instances are obtained from cipher lists or sessions; not directly constructed by user.
Opaque handle for an SSL/TLS session (resumption parameters, tickets, etc.). The struct is not defined here. Create and manage via SSL_SESSION_new(), SSL_new/handshake, or serialization APIs.
Opaque alias for a structure describing TLS signature algorithms. Not defined here.
Opaque configuration context for high-level SSL/SSL_CTX configuration commands. Not defined here. Created and freed via dedicated functions.
Concrete struct describing an SRTP protection profile for the use_srtp extension (RFC 5764). Holds a profile name and identifier.

objects.description: Enumeration of detailed internal handshake states for TLS/DTLS, used by SSL_get_state and related diagnostics. It is a typedef enum; use values directly, not as pointers. Pointer form here is for schema consistency.
Struct providing optional QUIC shutdown error details and reason string for SSL_shutdown_ex.
Struct specifying QUIC application error code when resetting a stream via SSL_stream_reset.
Struct used to query QUIC connection close information, including error code, frame type, reason text, and flags.
Struct used with SSL_poll to describe a polled object, desired events, and returned events. Wraps a BIO_POLL_DESCRIPTOR.

Legacy RAND method vtable structure used to plug in alternative random number generation implementations. Contains function pointers for seeding, generating bytes, cleanup, adding entropy, generating pseudorandom bytes, and status checks. Deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0; present for compatibility. Ownership and lifecycle are managed by callers; functions like RAND_set_rand_method() accept a const RAND_METHOD* and do not take ownership.

Context structure for the SHA-1 hash algorithm. Holds the 160-bit state (h0..h4), bit count (Nl, Nh), a 512-bit message block buffer (data), and the number of buffered bytes. Used with legacy SHA1_Init/Update/Final APIs. Details such as exact sizes depend on SHA_LONG being at least 32 bits.

Context structure for SHA-224 and SHA-256 algorithms. Contains 256-bit state (h[8]), bit count (Nl, Nh), a 512-bit message block buffer (data), buffered byte count (num), and output length (md_len). Used with legacy SHA224_/SHA256_ Init/Update/Final APIs.

Context structure for SHA-384 and SHA-512 algorithms. Contains 512-bit state (h[8]), 128-bit bit count (Nl, Nh), a 1024-bit message block buffer (u), buffered byte count (num), and output length (md_len). Relies on SHA_LONG64 being exactly 64 bits. Used with legacy SHA384_/SHA512_ Init/Update/Final APIs.

Underlying word type used by SHA-1 and SHA-256 family contexts and transforms. Must be at least 32 bits wide. Provided here as a macro definition; treated as an alias to unsigned int for compilation units including this header.

objects.definition:
#if (defined(_WIN32) || defined(_WIN64)) && !defined(__MINGW32__)
#define SHA_LONG64 unsigned __int64
#elif defined(__arch64__)
#define SHA_LONG64 unsigned long
#else
#define SHA_LONG64 unsigned long long
#endif
objects.description: Underlying 64-bit word type used by the SHA-512 family contexts and transforms. Required to be exactly 64 bits. Defined via platform-conditional macros to one of: unsigned __int64, unsigned long, or unsigned long long.

Expanded AES key schedule structure used by legacy/deprecated low-level OpenSSL AES APIs. Holds round keys (rd_key) for up to AES_MAXNR rounds and the number of rounds. Used for both encryption and decryption key schedules depending on how it is initialized. Details like the exact size of rd_key depend on AES_LONG and AES_MAXNR macros.

Opaque HMAC context type used by the OpenSSL HMAC APIs in this header. It is referenced for allocation, reset, free, copy, and parameter queries, but its actual structure/definition is not present in this header (it is defined elsewhere in OpenSSL).

Record describing a named OpenSSL object/method registered in the global OBJ_NAME table. Fields capture the object type (e.g., digest, cipher, pkey), whether the entry is an alias, the canonical name, and associated data string. Used by the OBJ_NAME_* registration and lookup APIs.

Opaque/incomplete node type used internally by the OpenSSL light-weight hash (lhash) implementation to represent a hash table bucket element. Only forward-declared here; layout is private to the library.

Opaque/incomplete handle for an OpenSSL dynamic hash table (lhash). Provides insertion, deletion, lookup, iteration, and stats helpers via the OPENSSL_LH_* API. The structure layout is intentionally hidden.
Function pointer type for element comparison callbacks used by OPENSSL_LHASH tables. Should return 0 for equality, <0, >0 for ordering as required by the hash table.

objects.definition: typedef int (*OPENSSL_LH_COMPFUNCTHUNK)(const void *, const void *, OPENSSL_LH_COMPFUNC cfn);
objects.description: Function pointer type for an adapter (“thunk”) that invokes a provided OPENSSL_LH_COMPFUNC with casting/bridging. Used internally to build type-safe wrappers.
Function pointer type for hash callbacks used by OPENSSL_LHASH tables. Must return a stable unsigned long hash for the key/object.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long (*OPENSSL_LH_HASHFUNCTHUNK)(const void *, OPENSSL_LH_HASHFUNC hfn);
objects.description: Function pointer type for an adapter (“thunk”) that invokes a provided OPENSSL_LH_HASHFUNC with casting/bridging. Used internally to build type-safe wrappers.
Function pointer type for 'doall' iteration callbacks applied to each element in an OPENSSL_LHASH without extra arguments.
Function pointer type for adapter that bridges to an OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNC during iteration with type casting.
Function pointer type for 'doall' iteration callbacks that accept an additional user-supplied argument.
Function pointer type for adapter that bridges to an OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG callback with type casting during iteration.

Type-safe wrapper struct tag for an lhash of OPENSSL_STRING (i.e., char* owned strings in OpenSSL style). The union enforces some compile-time checks; actual storage/layout is that of OPENSSL_LHASH when cast. Instances are created and manipulated via the lh_OPENSSL_STRING_* macros that forward to OPENSSL_LH_* APIs.

Type-safe wrapper struct tag for an lhash of OPENSSL_CSTRING (i.e., const char* string keys). The union enforces compile-time checks; actual operations are via lh_OPENSSL_CSTRING_* macros mapping to OPENSSL_LH_* APIs.

Opaque, type-safe stack wrapper for elements of type OPENSSL_STRING (i.e., char*). Implemented as a macro expanding to struct stack_st_OPENSSL_STRING, with accompanying sk_OPENSSL_STRING_* helpers for construction and manipulation. Actual structure layout is opaque and defined elsewhere.
Alias for a mutable NUL-terminated C string (char*). Used to distinguish stacks of strings and provide type-checked stack APIs.
Opaque, type-safe stack wrapper for elements of type OPENSSL_CSTRING (i.e., const char*). Opaque struct with helper macros sk_OPENSSL_CSTRING_* for creation and management.
Alias for an immutable NUL-terminated C string (const char*). Enables type-safe stack APIs for const strings.

Opaque, type-safe stack wrapper for elements of type OPENSSL_BLOCK (void*), intended for blocks of bytes (not NUL-terminated). Present only when OpenSSL 3.0 deprecations are enabled. The underlying struct layout is opaque; manipulation via sk_OPENSSL_BLOCK_* macros.
Alias for an untyped pointer representing a block of bytes (not NUL-terminated). Deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0 unless deprecations are enabled.
Opaque network address object used by OpenSSL BIO socket helpers. Only a typedef to an incomplete union is provided here; the real definition is elsewhere.
Opaque wrapper for address info results (akin to addrinfo) used by BIO lookup helpers. Only a typedef to an incomplete struct is provided here; the real definition is elsewhere.
Opaque type describing a BIO method (vtable). Only a typedef to an incomplete struct is provided here; methods are created and configured via BIO_meth_* APIs.
Message descriptor used with BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg. Holds a data pointer/length, optional peer and local BIO_ADDRs, and flags.
Arguments structure passed to multi-message send/receive callbacks for BIOs. References an array of BIO_MSG with stride, count, flags, and an output counter.
Descriptor describing what to poll on for a BIO: a socket fd, an SSL object, or a custom handle. Used with BIO_get_*poll_descriptor.

typedef int asn1_ps_func(BIO *b, unsigned char **pbuf, int *plen,
    void *parg);
objects.description: Function type used by the ASN1 BIO filter as prefix/suffix callbacks. Called to obtain or free prefix/suffix data buffers.
Callback function pointer type invoked to handle SCTP notifications on datagram BIOs when SCTP is enabled.

typedef int BIO_info_cb(BIO *, int, int);

objects.description: Information callback function type used by some BIOs for progress/trace notifications. The alias bio_info_cb exists for backward compatibility.
Deprecated pre-3.0 BIO operation callback function pointer type. Receives operation meta and return value for tracing/debugging.
Modern extended BIO operation callback function pointer type including sizes and processed byte counts.
Macro-generated opaque stack type for BIO pointers. The full struct is opaque; access via sk_BIO_* macros.
SCTP send info structure used with datagram SCTP BIOs, containing stream id, flags, PPID, and context. Only present when SCTP support is enabled.
SCTP receive info structure for datagram SCTP BIOs, holding stream/session ids, flags, PPID, TSN, cum TSN, and context. Present with SCTP enabled.
SCTP partial reliability info structure for datagram SCTP BIOs, including PR-SCTP policy and associated value. Present with SCTP enabled.
Enumeration controlling how BIO_parse_hostserv prioritizes host vs service parsing.
Enumeration selecting client vs server semantics for BIO_lookup/BIO_lookup_ex.
Union used with BIO_sock_info to return socket-related info such as peer address.
Enumeration specifying which socket info is requested via BIO_sock_info.
Primary typedef for a BIO info callback function. See also alias bio_info_cb.

Resizable buffer descriptor used by OpenSSL. Tracks current length, underlying data pointer, allocated capacity (max), and flags (e.g., secure allocation). Public API functions allocate, grow, and free this buffer. The data field may be reallocated by grow operations; users should treat it as owned by BUF_MEM and not free it directly.
Opaque handle to a loaded OpenSSL provider within a given OSSL_LIB_CTX. This header only declares it via pointer usage; the struct definition is not present here and is managed internally by OpenSSL.
Opaque OpenSSL library context object used to scope provider loading and configuration. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Opaque/SDK-defined parameter descriptor array type used to pass name-typed values to/from providers. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Descriptor type for algorithm implementations exposed by a provider. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere. Note functions here return const OSSL_ALGORITHM *.
Function callback type used by OpenSSL for enumerations like capability queries. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Dispatch table entry type used by providers to expose function IDs and pointers. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Function pointer type for built-in provider initialization routine. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Opaque handle to an OCSP certificate identifier (hashes of issuer name/key plus serial). The structure is not defined here; treat as an opaque ASN.1 type managed via provided APIs.
Opaque handle representing a single certificate status request within an OCSP request. Contains an OCSP_CERTID and optional extensions.
Opaque internal container for the tbsRequest portion of an OCSP request (request list, requesterName, extensions). Not directly constructed by callers.
Opaque handle to the optional signature structure attached to an OCSP request (algorithm, signature bits, certs).
Opaque handle for an OCSP request message. Holds one or more OCSP_ONEREQ entries plus optional signature and extensions.
Opaque ASN.1 container for responseBytes inside OCSPResponse (responseType OID and the actual response octets).

objects.definition: /* forward-declared via STACK macros and ASN.1 decls; concrete typedef missing above but implied by DECLARE_ASN1_FUNCTIONS */
objects.description: Opaque handle identifying an OCSP responder, either by name or by key hash. Used in BasicOCSPResponse to bind the signer identity.
Opaque ASN.1 structure conveying revocation time and optional reason for a revoked cert status.
Opaque ASN.1 CHOICE describing certificate status: good, revoked (with OCSP_REVOKEDINFO), or unknown.
Opaque handle for a SingleResponse inside a BasicOCSPResponse, containing the status of one certificate plus timing and extensions.
Opaque handle for the tbsResponseData of a BasicOCSPResponse (responderID, producedAt, responses, extensions).
Opaque handle for BasicOCSPResponse content type (tbsResponseData, signatureAlgorithm, signature, and optional certs).
Opaque ASN.1 structure for the OCSP CRL ID extension (crlUrl, crlNum, crlTime).
Opaque ASN.1 structure for the ServiceLocator extension indicating alternative OCSP responder locations for an issuer.

objects.description: Opaque handle for the top-level OCSPResponse message (responseStatus and optional responseBytes).
