objects.description: Type-safe STACK_OF aliases generated for various OCSP object pointers. Each is an OpenSSL stack of the corresponding pointer type. Construction uses OPENSSL_sk_* functions via the provided macros.
Opaque store context handle representing an open STORE channel used to load or manage objects from a URI or BIO. The struct is forward-declared here and defined privately within OpenSSL.

Opaque container for a single item returned by OSSL_STORE (name, params, public key, private key, certificate, CRL, or secret key). The concrete struct is not defined in this header. Items are created via OSSL_STORE_INFO_new* helpers and freed with OSSL_STORE_INFO_free.

Opaque search-criteria object used to filter results from a STORE loader (by name, issuer+serial, key fingerprint, or alias). Constructed via OSSL_STORE_SEARCH_by_* and freed with OSSL_STORE_SEARCH_free.
Opaque provider-discoverable loader implementation handle for a STORE scheme. Instances are fetched from providers or (deprecated) constructed manually. This header exposes no struct definition.

objects.definition:
/* struct ossl_store_loader_ctx_st is defined differently by each loader */
typedef struct ossl_store_loader_ctx_st OSSL_STORE_LOADER_CTX;
objects.description: Opaque, loader-specific per-open context used by legacy/deprecated STORE_LOADER method-table APIs. Actual layout is defined by each loader implementation, not in this header.
Function pointer typedef for a callback that can transform or discard an OSSL_STORE_INFO item during loading. Return NULL to drop the item.

objects.definition:
typedef OSSL_STORE_LOADER_CTX *(*OSSL_STORE_open_fn)(const OSSL_STORE_LOADER *loader, const char *uri,
    const UI_METHOD *ui_method, void *ui_data);
objects.description: Deprecated function-pointer typedef for a loader's open routine given a URI, returning a loader-specific context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for a loader's extended open routine with libctx/propq.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for attaching a loader to an existing BIO, returning a loader context.

objects.definition: typedef int (*OSSL_STORE_ctrl_fn)(OSSL_STORE_LOADER_CTX *ctx, int cmd, va_list args);
objects.description: Deprecated function-pointer typedef for loader-specific control operations on a loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for indicating an expected type to the loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for applying search criteria in the loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for loading the next OSSL_STORE_INFO item from the loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for checking end-of-data in the loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for checking error status in the loader context.
Deprecated function-pointer typedef for closing and freeing a loader context.

Opaque handle to a Time-Stamp MessageImprint structure (ASN.1 TS_MSG_IMPRINT). Represents the hash algorithm identifier and the hashed message for a timestamp request/response. The actual struct layout is hidden in the library.
Opaque handle to a Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) request object (ASN.1 TS_REQ). Holds the version, message imprint, policy, nonce, cert request flag, and extensions of a timestamp request.
Opaque handle to the TS_ACCURACY ASN.1 structure indicating timestamp accuracy (seconds, millis, micros).
Opaque handle to a Time-Stamp Token Info structure (ASN.1 TSTInfo). Contains policy, message imprint, serial number, time, accuracy, ordering flag, nonce, TSA name and extensions.
Opaque handle to the PKIX TS StatusInfo structure containing status code, optional status text, and failure info bit string.
Opaque handle to a Time-Stamp response object (ASN.1 TimeStampResp), which includes status info and an optional PKCS7 token encapsulating TSTInfo.
Opaque context used to configure and generate timestamp responses (signer cert/key, policies, digests, accuracy, callbacks, flags).
Opaque context used for verifying timestamp responses or tokens, holding verification flags, input data or imprint, trusted store/certs, policy, and related parameters.
Function pointer type for a callback that returns a unique serial number (ASN1_INTEGER*) for a response, given a TS_RESP_CTX and user data.

objects.definition: typedef int (*TS_time_cb)(struct TS_resp_ctx *, void *, long *sec, long *usec);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback that fills seconds and microseconds since the epoch for timestamping. Returns non-zero on success.
Function pointer type for a callback to process a requested X509 extension while building a TST_INFO. Non-zero means processed; zero indicates error and status/failure info should be set.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new OpenSSL read/write lock object used for intra-process synchronization.
requirements: Call CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free to release the returned lock when no longer needed.
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL to detect allocation failure before use.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock
functions.description: Acquires the lock for shared (read) access on the given CRYPTO_RWLOCK.
requirements: lock must be a valid CRYPTO_RWLOCK obtained from CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new.
Do not pass NULL for lock.
Must be paired with CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock when the read section ends.
Return value must be checked: nonzero indicates success; zero indicates failure (function is marked __owur).

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock
functions.description: Acquires the lock for exclusive (write) access on the given CRYPTO_RWLOCK.
requirements: lock must be a valid CRYPTO_RWLOCK obtained from CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new.
Do not pass NULL for lock.
Must be paired with CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock after the critical section.
Return value must be checked (function is marked __owur).

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired read or write lock.
requirements: lock must be a valid CRYPTO_RWLOCK and currently held by the calling thread (via CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock or CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock).
Return value should be checked for success/failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free
functions.description: Frees a CRYPTO_RWLOCK allocated by CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new.
requirements: lock must either be NULL or a lock allocated by CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new.
The lock must not be held by any thread when freed.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_add
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_atomic_add(int *val, int amount, int *ret, CRYPTO_RWLOCK *lock);
functions.description: Atomically adds amount to *val, optionally using the provided lock, and stores the new value in *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to an int.
ret must be a valid pointer to an int if non-NULL; if provided, it receives the result.
lock, if required by the platform, must be a valid CRYPTO_RWLOCK; passing NULL may be unsupported on some platforms (per OpenSSL patterns).
Return value should be checked to detect failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_add64
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_atomic_add64(uint64_t *val, uint64_t op, uint64_t *ret, CRYPTO_RWLOCK *lock);
functions.description: Atomically adds op to *val, storing the new value in *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
ret must be a valid pointer to uint64_t if non-NULL.
lock must be a valid CRYPTO_RWLOCK when required by the platform.
Return value must be checked for success.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_and
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_atomic_and(uint64_t *val, uint64_t op, uint64_t *ret, CRYPTO_RWLOCK *lock);
functions.description: Atomically applies bitwise AND of *val with op, storing the result in *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
ret must be a valid pointer to uint64_t if non-NULL.
lock must be valid when required by platform.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_or
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_atomic_or(uint64_t *val, uint64_t op, uint64_t *ret, CRYPTO_RWLOCK *lock);
functions.description: Atomically applies bitwise OR of *val with op, storing the result in *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
ret must be a valid pointer to uint64_t if non-NULL.
lock must be valid when required by platform.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_load
functions.description: Atomically loads the value at *val into *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
ret must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
lock must be valid when required by the platform.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_load_int
functions.description: Atomically loads the value at *val into *ret.
requirements: val must be a valid pointer to int.
ret must be a valid pointer to int.
lock must be valid when required by the platform.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_atomic_store
functions.description: Atomically stores val into *dst.
requirements: dst must be a valid pointer to uint64_t.
lock must be valid when required by the platform.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strlcpy
functions.signature: size_t OPENSSL_strlcpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t siz);
functions.description: Safe string copy: copies src to dst of size siz, NUL-terminating unless siz is 0; returns the length of src.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer of at least siz bytes.
src must be a NUL-terminated string.
If siz is 0, dst may be NULL; otherwise it must be non-NULL.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strlcat
functions.signature: size_t OPENSSL_strlcat(char *dst, const char *src, size_t siz);
functions.description: Safe string concatenation: appends src to dst of total size siz, NUL-terminating unless siz is 0; returns initial length of dst plus length of src.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer of at least siz bytes and contain a NUL-terminated string.
src must be a NUL-terminated string.
If siz is 0, dst may be NULL; otherwise it must be non-NULL.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strnlen
functions.description: Returns the length of the string str, limited to at most maxlen.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer; it need not be NUL-terminated if a NUL occurs before maxlen.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strtoul
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_strtoul(const char *str, char **endptr, int base, unsigned long *num);
functions.description: Parses an unsigned long from the NUL-terminated string str with the given base, storing the result in *num and optionally updating endptr; returns 1 on success, 0 on error (per OpenSSL conventions).
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
num must be a valid pointer to unsigned long.
If endptr is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to char* to receive the parse end position.
base must be a valid base as per strtoul semantics (e.g., 0 or 2–36).
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_buf2hexstr_ex
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_buf2hexstr_ex(char *str, size_t str_n, size_t *strlength, const unsigned char *buf, size_t buflen, const char sep);
functions.description: Converts a binary buffer to a printable hexadecimal string, optionally inserting sep between bytes, writing to str with capacity str_n and returning the produced length in *strlength.
requirements: If str is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least str_n bytes.
If str is NULL, str_n should be 0 (typical pattern); exact behavior not documented here.
buf must point to buflen bytes of input.
strlength, if non-NULL, must be valid to receive the output length.
Return value must be checked for success.

functions.name: OPENSSL_buf2hexstr
functions.description: Allocates and returns a newly allocated NUL-terminated hex string representation of the input buffer.
requirements: buf must point to buflen bytes of input (buf may be NULL if buflen==0).
Caller must free the returned string with OPENSSL_free/CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_hexstr2buf_ex
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_hexstr2buf_ex(unsigned char *buf, size_t buf_n, size_t *buflen, const char *str, const char sep);
functions.description: Parses a hex string (optionally containing separator sep) into binary, writing to buf up to buf_n bytes, and returns the number of bytes via *buflen.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least buf_n bytes when buf is non-NULL.
str must be a valid NUL-terminated string containing hexadecimal characters (and optional separators).
buflen must be a valid pointer if non-NULL to receive output length.
Return value must be checked for success and potential truncation/format errors.

functions.name: OPENSSL_hexstr2buf
functions.description: Allocates and returns a buffer containing the binary decoding of a hex string, optionally returning the output length via buflen.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If buflen is non-NULL, it must be valid to receive the output length.
Caller must free the returned buffer with OPENSSL_free/CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return indicating parse or allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_hexchar2int
functions.description: Converts a single hexadecimal character to its integer value (0–15) or returns an error indicator if invalid.
requirements: Input c should be an ASCII hex digit (0-9, a-f, A-F) for a defined result.
Caller should handle negative/error return for non-hex characters (exact value unspecified here).

functions.name: OPENSSL_strcasecmp
functions.description: Case-insensitive string comparison of s1 and s2, returning an integer similar to strcasecmp semantics.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strncasecmp
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_strncasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of up to n characters of s1 and s2.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings (or at least n bytes accessible).

functions.name: OPENSSL_version_major
functions.description: Returns the library’s major version number.

functions.name: OPENSSL_version_minor
functions.description: Returns the library’s minor version number.

functions.name: OPENSSL_version_patch
functions.description: Returns the library’s patch version number.

functions.name: OPENSSL_version_pre_release
functions.description: Returns a string with pre-release version info, or an empty string if none.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: OPENSSL_version_build_metadata
functions.description: Returns a string with build metadata for the library, or an empty string if none.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: OpenSSL_version_num
functions.description: Returns the packed numeric OpenSSL version number (e.g., 0xMNNFFPPSL).

functions.name: OpenSSL_version
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing version/build info selected by type (e.g., OPENSSL_VERSION, OPENSSL_CFLAGS).
requirements: type must be one of the OPENSSL_* defines documented in the header (e.g., OPENSSL_VERSION, OPENSSL_CFLAGS, etc.).
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: OPENSSL_info
functions.description: Returns a string containing process or build-time information designated by the OPENSSL_INFO_* type.
requirements: type must be one of the OPENSSL_INFO_* constants (e.g., OPENSSL_INFO_CONFIG_DIR, etc.).
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: OPENSSL_issetugid
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the process is running with elevated or modified user/group IDs (set-user-ID or set-group-ID).

functions.name: CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index
functions.signature: __owur int CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index(int class_index, long argl, void *argp, CRYPTO_EX_new *new_func, CRYPTO_EX_dup *dup_func, CRYPTO_EX_free *free_func);
functions.description: Reserves a new ex_data index for the specified class and optionally registers callbacks for new/dup/free events.
requirements: class_index must be one of the CRYPTO_EX_INDEX_* values defined.
Callbacks (if provided) must match the declared types.
Return value must be checked for success (nonnegative index vs error).

functions.name: CRYPTO_free_ex_index
functions.description: Releases an ex_data index previously obtained for the given class.
requirements: class_index must be a valid CRYPTO_EX_INDEX_* value.
idx must be an index previously returned by CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index for the same class.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_new_ex_data
functions.description: Initializes a CRYPTO_EX_DATA structure for a new object of the given class, invoking any registered new callbacks.
requirements: ad must point to a CRYPTO_EX_DATA to initialize.
class_index must be a valid CRYPTO_EX_INDEX_* value.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_dup_ex_data
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_dup_ex_data(int class_index, CRYPTO_EX_DATA *to, const CRYPTO_EX_DATA *from);
functions.description: Duplicates ex_data from one object to another of the same class, invoking registered dup callbacks.
requirements: class_index must be valid for both objects’ class.
to and from must be valid CRYPTO_EX_DATA pointers.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_free_ex_data
functions.description: Frees resources associated with a CRYPTO_EX_DATA for an object of the specified class, invoking registered free callbacks.
requirements: ad must be a valid CRYPTO_EX_DATA previously initialized.
class_index must match the class used at initialization.

functions.name: CRYPTO_alloc_ex_data
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_alloc_ex_data(int class_index, void *obj, CRYPTO_EX_DATA *ad, int idx);
functions.description: Allocates a single ex_data item at the given index for the object’s CRYPTO_EX_DATA.
requirements: ad must be initialized for the given class_index.
idx must be a valid ex_data index for the class.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_set_ex_data
functions.description: Sets a value at index idx in the CRYPTO_EX_DATA structure.
requirements: ad must be initialized.
idx must be a valid index for ad’s class.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_get_ex_data
functions.description: Retrieves the value at index idx from the CRYPTO_EX_DATA structure.
requirements: ad must be initialized.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: CRYPTO_set_mem_functions
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_set_mem_functions(CRYPTO_malloc_fn malloc_fn, CRYPTO_realloc_fn realloc_fn, CRYPTO_free_fn free_fn);
functions.description: Overrides the library’s memory allocation, reallocation, and free callbacks.
requirements: malloc_fn, realloc_fn, and free_fn must be valid function pointers implementing the required semantics.
Must be called before any allocations take place in the library (typical requirement for such APIs; exact timing not documented here).
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_get_mem_functions
functions.description: Retrieves the library’s current memory allocation callbacks.
requirements: malloc_fn, realloc_fn, and free_fn pointers must be non-NULL and writable.

functions.name: CRYPTO_malloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_malloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates num bytes of memory and returns a pointer to it (tracking file/line for diagnostics).
requirements: num may be zero; behavior follows OpenSSL allocation conventions.
Returned pointer must be freed with CRYPTO_free/OPENSSL_free.
Check for NULL return on failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_zalloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_zalloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates num bytes of zero-initialized memory.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with CRYPTO_free/OPENSSL_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_malloc_array
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_malloc_array(size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates an array of num elements of size bytes (with overflow checking).
requirements: num*size must fit in size_t; overflow causes failure.
Returned pointer must be freed with CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_calloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_calloc(size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array of num elements of size bytes.
requirements: num*size must fit in size_t; overflow causes failure.
Returned pointer must be freed with CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_aligned_alloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_aligned_alloc(size_t num, size_t align, void **freeptr, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates num bytes with a specified alignment, returning the aligned address and an auxiliary pointer via freeptr for freeing.
requirements: align must be a valid alignment (typically power-of-two); exact constraints not specified here.
freeptr must be a valid pointer to void* to receive the pointer to pass to CRYPTO_free.
Returned pointer must be freed using CRYPTO_free with the pointer stored at *freeptr (per OpenSSL aligned alloc pattern).
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_aligned_alloc_array
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_aligned_alloc_array(size_t num, size_t size, size_t align, void **freeptr, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates an aligned array of num elements of size bytes with the given alignment, returning an aligned pointer and a free handle via freeptr.
requirements: num*size must not overflow size_t.
align must be a valid alignment.
freeptr must be a valid pointer to void*.
Use CRYPTO_free on the pointer stored in *freeptr to free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_memdup
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_memdup(const void *str, size_t siz, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Duplicates a memory block of siz bytes from str into a newly allocated buffer.
requirements: If siz > 0, str must point to at least siz bytes.
Caller must free the returned buffer with CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_strdup
functions.signature: char *CRYPTO_strdup(const char *str, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Duplicates a NUL-terminated string using OpenSSL’s allocator.
requirements: str must be a NUL-terminated string (may be NULL per implementation; behavior unspecified here).
Caller must free with CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_strndup
functions.signature: char *CRYPTO_strndup(const char *str, size_t s, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Duplicates up to s bytes from the string str into a new NUL-terminated string.
requirements: str must point to at least s bytes or to a NUL-terminated string shorter than s.
Caller must free with CRYPTO_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_free(void *ptr, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by an OpenSSL allocation routine.
requirements: ptr must either be NULL or a pointer returned by an OpenSSL allocator compatible with CRYPTO_free.
Do not use standard free() on memory allocated by OpenSSL allocators.

functions.name: CRYPTO_clear_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_clear_free(void *ptr, size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Overwrites num bytes at ptr (to cleanse sensitive data) and then frees the buffer.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer to a buffer of at least num bytes allocated by an OpenSSL allocator compatible with CRYPTO_free.
num should match the allocation size for complete cleansing (cannot be verified by the function).

functions.name: CRYPTO_realloc
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_realloc(void *addr, size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Changes the size of the allocation at addr to num bytes, returning the (possibly moved) pointer.
requirements: addr must be NULL or a pointer allocated by an OpenSSL allocator compatible with CRYPTO_free.
On failure, returns NULL and the original allocation remains valid; caller must handle this.
If num is 0, behavior follows OpenSSL conventions (may free and return NULL).

functions.name: CRYPTO_clear_realloc
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_clear_realloc(void *addr, size_t old_num, size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Like CRYPTO_realloc but ensures that any reduced portion (old_num - num) is cleansed before being released.
requirements: addr must be a valid OpenSSL allocation or NULL.
old_num should reflect the previous allocation size for correct cleansing semantics.
Check for NULL return on failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_realloc_array
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_realloc_array(void *addr, size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Resizes an array allocation to num elements of size bytes with overflow checking.
requirements: addr must be a valid OpenSSL allocation or NULL.
num*size must not overflow size_t.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_clear_realloc_array
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_clear_realloc_array(void *addr, size_t old_num, size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Resizes an array allocation with cleansing of any truncated portion, with overflow checking.
requirements: addr must be a valid OpenSSL allocation or NULL.
old_num should reflect the previous element count for cleansing.
num*size must not overflow size_t.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init
functions.description: Initializes the secure memory allocator with a backing pool of size sz and a minimum allocation size minsize.
requirements: Must be called before using secure allocation functions.
Return value must be checked for success.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_done
functions.description: Shuts down the secure memory allocator, releasing its resources if possible.
requirements: All secure allocations must be freed before calling.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_secure_malloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates num bytes from the secure memory pool (if initialized).
requirements: Secure allocator must have been initialized via CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init.
Caller must free with CRYPTO_secure_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_zalloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_secure_zalloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized secure memory of num bytes.
requirements: Secure allocator must be initialized.
Caller must free with CRYPTO_secure_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_array
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_secure_malloc_array(size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates an array in secure memory for num elements of size bytes with overflow checking.
requirements: Secure allocator must be initialized.
num*size must not overflow.
Caller must free with CRYPTO_secure_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_calloc
functions.signature: OSSL_CRYPTO_ALLOC void *CRYPTO_secure_calloc(size_t num, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized secure memory for an array of num elements of size bytes.
requirements: Secure allocator must be initialized.
num*size must not overflow.
Caller must free with CRYPTO_secure_free.
Check for NULL return.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_secure_free(void *ptr, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated from the secure allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or a pointer returned by a CRYPTO_secure_* allocator.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_clear_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_secure_clear_free(void *ptr, size_t num, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Cleanses num bytes at ptr and frees the secure allocation.
requirements: ptr must be a secure allocation pointer.
num should reflect the allocation size for full cleansing.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_allocated
functions.description: Returns nonzero if ptr points to memory managed by the secure allocator.
requirements: ptr may be NULL; function returns 0 for non-secure or NULL pointers.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_initialized
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the secure memory allocator has been initialized.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_actual_size
functions.description: Returns the actual usable size of a secure allocation pointed to by ptr.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer to a secure allocation.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_used
functions.description: Returns the total amount of secure memory currently in use.

functions.name: OPENSSL_cleanse
functions.description: Overwrites len bytes at ptr to cleanse sensitive data from memory.
requirements: ptr must point to at least len writable bytes.

functions.name: CRYPTO_get_alloc_counts
functions.description: Retrieves internal allocation, reallocation, and free counters for debugging builds (when memory debug is enabled).
requirements: mcount, rcount, and fcount must be valid writable pointers.
Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined.

functions.name: CRYPTO_set_mem_debug
functions.description: Enables or disables memory-debug mode (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_ctrl
functions.description: Controls memory-debug behavior/mode (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
mode must be a valid control mode per OpenSSL memory debug API (details not included here).
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_debug_push
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_mem_debug_push(const char *info, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Pushes a debugging info frame for subsequent allocations (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
info must be a valid string pointer.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_debug_pop
functions.description: Pops the last debugging info frame (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_debug_malloc
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_mem_debug_malloc(void *addr, size_t num, int flag, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Debug hook to record a malloc event (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
addr must be the allocated address or NULL on failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_debug_realloc
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_mem_debug_realloc(void *addr1, void *addr2, size_t num, int flag, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Debug hook to record a realloc event (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
addr1 is old address; addr2 is new address (or NULL on failure).

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_debug_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_mem_debug_free(void *addr, int flag, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Debug hook to record a free event (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
addr may be NULL.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_leaks_cb
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_mem_leaks_cb(int (*cb)(const char *str, size_t len, void *u), void *u);
functions.description: Reports memory leaks via a user-supplied callback (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
cb must be a valid function pointer taking (str,len,u).
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_leaks_fp
functions.description: Reports memory leaks to a FILE* stream (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined, and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
FILE* must be valid.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_mem_leaks
functions.description: Reports memory leaks to a BIO (deprecated in 3.0).
requirements: Only available when OPENSSL_NO_CRYPTO_MDEBUG is not defined and not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
bio must be a valid BIO.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_die
functions.signature: ossl_noreturn void OPENSSL_die(const char *assertion, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Terminates the process, reporting an assertion failure message, file, and line.
requirements: This function does not return (noreturn).
Parameters should describe the failed assertion and source location.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isservice
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the process is running as a service (platform-specific).

functions.name: OPENSSL_init
functions.description: Performs basic library initialization.
requirements: Should be called early in process startup if explicit initialization is desired.

functions.name: OPENSSL_fork_prepare
functions.description: Prepares OpenSSL for a fork by acquiring internal locks (deprecated in 3.0; UNIX only).
requirements: Only available on UNIX platforms and when not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
Should be called in the parent before fork().

functions.name: OPENSSL_fork_parent
functions.description: Releases resources in the parent after fork (deprecated in 3.0; UNIX only).
requirements: Only available on UNIX and when not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
Should be called in the parent after fork().

functions.name: OPENSSL_fork_child
functions.description: Reinitializes or releases resources in the child after fork (deprecated in 3.0; UNIX only).
requirements: Only available on UNIX and when not disabled by OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
Should be called in the child after fork().

functions.name: OPENSSL_gmtime
functions.description: Thread-safe gmtime: converts timer (seconds since epoch) to broken-down UTC time stored in result and returns result.
requirements: timer and result must be valid pointers.
result must point to a writable struct tm.

functions.name: OPENSSL_gmtime_adj
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_gmtime_adj(struct tm *tm, int offset_day, long offset_sec);
functions.description: Adjusts a struct tm by offset_day days and offset_sec seconds.
requirements: tm must be a valid pointer to a struct tm to be modified.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_gmtime_diff
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_gmtime_diff(int *pday, int *psec, const struct tm *from, const struct tm *to);
functions.description: Computes the difference between two times, returning day and second differences via pday and psec.
requirements: pday and psec must be valid writable pointers.
from and to must be valid pointers to struct tm.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_memcmp
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_memcmp(const void *in_a, const void *in_b, size_t len);
functions.description: Constant-time memory comparison: returns 0 iff the len bytes at in_a and in_b are equal; nonzero otherwise. Execution time depends only on len, not contents.
requirements: in_a and in_b must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: OPENSSL_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up OpenSSL library state and frees resources.
requirements: Should be called during process shutdown when explicit cleanup is desired.

functions.name: OPENSSL_init_crypto
functions.description: Initializes the OpenSSL crypto library with the specified options and optional settings object.
requirements: opts is a bitmask of OPENSSL_INIT_* flags defined in the header.
settings may be NULL or a valid pointer created by OPENSSL_INIT_new/initialized accordingly.
Return value must be checked for success.

functions.name: OPENSSL_atexit
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked at OpenSSL cleanup/exit.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer.
Return value should be checked for registration success.

functions.name: OPENSSL_thread_stop
functions.description: Releases thread-local OpenSSL resources for the calling thread.
requirements: Should be called when a thread using OpenSSL is about to exit.

functions.name: OPENSSL_thread_stop_ex
functions.description: Releases thread-local OpenSSL resources for the calling thread within the specified library context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX or NULL for default, per OpenSSL patterns (exact behavior not specified here).

functions.name: OPENSSL_INIT_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS object for configuring initialization.
requirements: Check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.
Caller must free with OPENSSL_INIT_free.

functions.name: OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_filename
functions.description: Sets a configuration filename on the settings object for later use during initialization.
requirements: settings must be a valid OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS pointer.
config_filename must be a valid string pointer.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_file_flags
functions.description: Sets configuration file flags on the settings object.
requirements: settings must be a valid OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS pointer.
flags must be a valid combination of configuration flags accepted by OpenSSL (details not provided here).

functions.name: OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_appname
functions.description: Sets the application name used when loading configuration via the settings object.
requirements: settings must be valid.
config_appname must be a valid string pointer.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OPENSSL_INIT_free
functions.description: Frees an OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS object created by OPENSSL_INIT_new.
requirements: settings may be NULL; otherwise must be a pointer returned by OPENSSL_INIT_new.
Do not use the settings object after freeing.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_run_once
functions.description: Executes init exactly once per-process (or per address space) for the given once control.
requirements: once must point to a CRYPTO_ONCE initialized to CRYPTO_ONCE_STATIC_INIT or previously used.
init must be a valid function pointer.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_init_local
functions.description: Initializes a thread-local storage key with an optional cleanup destructor.
requirements: key must be a valid pointer to CRYPTO_THREAD_LOCAL.
cleanup may be NULL or a valid function pointer.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local
functions.description: Retrieves the thread-local value associated with key for the calling thread.
requirements: key must be initialized with CRYPTO_THREAD_init_local.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_set_local
functions.description: Sets the thread-local value for key in the calling thread.
requirements: key must be initialized.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_cleanup_local
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a thread-local key, invoking its destructor as appropriate.
requirements: key must be initialized.
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_get_current_id
functions.description: Returns an identifier for the calling thread.

functions.name: CRYPTO_THREAD_compare_id
functions.description: Compares two thread identifiers; returns nonzero if equal, zero otherwise (per OpenSSL patterns).

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new OpenSSL library context for algorithm/provider operations isolated from the global default.
requirements: Check for NULL return and free with OSSL_LIB_CTX_free when done.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_from_dispatch
functions.description: Creates a new library context from a provider core handle and dispatch table (used inside providers).
requirements: handle and in must be valid pointers appropriate for the provider environment.
Check for NULL return; free with OSSL_LIB_CTX_free.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_child
functions.description: Creates a new child library context associated with a provider core handle and dispatch table.
requirements: handle and in must be valid pointers in the provider context.
Check for NULL return; free with OSSL_LIB_CTX_free.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_load_config
functions.description: Loads an OpenSSL configuration file into the specified library context.
requirements: ctx may be NULL to use the default context or a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX.
config_file must be a valid filename string (may be NULL to use defaults per OpenSSL behavior; exact details not included here).
Return value should be checked.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a library context created by OSSL_LIB_CTX_new*.
requirements: Argument may be NULL; otherwise must be a context allocated by OSSL_LIB_CTX_new/OSSL_LIB_CTX_new_*.
Do not use the context after freeing.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_get0_global_default
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the process’s global default library context (non-owning).
requirements: Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default
functions.description: Sets libctx as the process’s global default library context and returns the previous default.
requirements: libctx may be NULL to reset to built-in default (per OpenSSL patterns; exact behavior not detailed here).
Returned previous default must not be freed unless the caller owns it.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_get_conf_diagnostics
functions.description: Gets the configuration diagnostics flag for the given library context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context or NULL for default (per OpenSSL patterns; exact behavior not detailed).

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_set_conf_diagnostics
functions.description: Enables or disables configuration diagnostics on the given library context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context or NULL for default.
value controls diagnostics; acceptable values are not detailed here.

functions.name: OSSL_sleep
functions.description: Sleeps the current thread for the specified number of milliseconds.
requirements: This is a blocking call; millis is the sleep duration.

functions.name: OSSL_LIB_CTX_get_data
functions.description: Retrieves per-context data associated with the given index from the specified library context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context or NULL to indicate the default context (per OpenSSL patterns).
index must be a valid data index established by OpenSSL internals or providers.

functions.name: ERR_new
functions.description: Starts a new error record on the current thread’s OpenSSL error queue. Typically called before providing debug/location and formatted message via ERR_set_debug and ERR_set_error/ERR_vset_error (implicitly also done by ERR_raise/ERR_raise_data).
requirements: Must be called on a thread where an error is being recorded; typically immediately before ERR_set_debug and ERR_set_error/ERR_vset_error.
Thread-affine: operates on the calling thread’s error queue.

functions.name: ERR_set_debug
functions.signature: void ERR_set_debug(const char *file, int line, const char *func);
functions.description: Associates source location metadata (file, line, function) with the most recent in-progress error on the calling thread. Typically used after ERR_new and before setting the formatted message.
requirements: file should point to a NUL-terminated filename string or be NULL if unknown.
func should point to a NUL-terminated function-name string or be NULL if unknown.
line should be a non-negative line number.
Must be called after ERR_new to affect the current error under construction.
Thread-affine: affects the calling thread’s error queue.

functions.name: ERR_set_error
functions.signature: void ERR_set_error(int lib, int reason, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Finalizes the current error by setting its library and reason code and an optional formatted message (printf-style). Used after ERR_new/ERR_set_debug. ERR_raise/ERR_raise_data macro sequence calls into this function automatically.
requirements: lib must be a valid OpenSSL library code (e.g., ERR_LIB_EVP, ERR_LIB_SSL, etc.).
reason must be a valid reason code for the library or a common reason (combined with flags as per ERR_* macros).
If fmt is non-NULL, it must be a valid printf-style format string and the variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Must be called after ERR_new for the current error being built.
Thread-affine: records on the calling thread’s error queue.

functions.name: ERR_vset_error
functions.signature: void ERR_vset_error(int lib, int reason, const char *fmt, va_list args);
functions.description: Variant of ERR_set_error that takes a va_list for formatted message construction. Intended for wrappers that already manage a va_list.
requirements: lib and reason follow the same rules as ERR_set_error.
If fmt is non-NULL, it must be a valid printf-style format string; args must be an initialized va_list matching fmt.
va_list lifetime must be valid for the duration of the call.
Must be called after ERR_new for the current error being built.
Thread-affine: records on the calling thread’s error queue.

functions.name: ERR_set_error_data
functions.description: Attaches auxiliary data text to the most recent error on the calling thread. Ownership and interpretation are controlled by flags (e.g., ERR_TXT_MALLOCED, ERR_TXT_STRING).
requirements: Must be called after starting an error (e.g., after ERR_new/ERR_set_error).
If flags includes ERR_TXT_MALLOCED, data must be heap-allocated; ownership transfers to OpenSSL which will free it.
If flags includes ERR_TXT_STRING, data must be a NUL-terminated string.
data may be NULL to clear or when no data is provided (behavior beyond this is implementation-defined).
Thread-affine: affects the calling thread’s current error.

functions.name: ERR_get_error
functions.description: Pops and returns the earliest error code from the calling thread’s error queue, removing it from the queue. Returns 0 if no error is present.
requirements: Call on the same thread where errors were raised.
Check for return value 0 to detect an empty queue.
Use ERR_LIB_* and helpers (ERR_GET_LIB/ERR_GET_REASON) to decode the returned code.

functions.name: ERR_get_error_all
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_get_error_all(const char **file, int *line, const char **func, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Pops and returns the earliest error code from the calling thread’s queue and optionally retrieves associated metadata (file, line, func, data, flags). Any output pointer may be NULL to ignore that field.
requirements: Any of file, line, func, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers (file, func, data) point to internal storage valid until the error queue is modified; copy if needed beyond that.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_get_error_line
functions.description: Deprecated (3.0): Pops and returns the earliest error code and optionally its source file and line. Prefer ERR_get_error_all.
requirements: file and line may be NULL to ignore.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.
Deprecated: avoid in new code.

functions.name: ERR_get_error_line_data
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_get_error_line_data(const char **file, int *line, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Deprecated (3.0): Pops and returns the earliest error code and optionally file, line, attached data text, and data flags. Prefer ERR_get_error_all.
requirements: Any of file, line, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned data pointer refers to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.
Deprecated: avoid in new code.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the earliest error code from the calling thread’s error queue. Returns 0 if none.
requirements: Non-destructive: does not pop the error.
Check for 0 to detect no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error_line
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the earliest error code and optionally its source file and line.
requirements: file and line may be NULL to ignore.
Pointers returned may refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error_func
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the earliest error code and optionally the function name associated with it.
requirements: func may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error_data
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the earliest error code and optionally the attached error data text and its flags.
requirements: data and flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned data pointer refers to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error_all
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_peek_error_all(const char **file, int *line, const char **func, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the earliest error code and optionally retrieves file, line, function, data text, and flags.
requirements: Any of file, line, func, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_error_line_data
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_peek_error_line_data(const char **file, int *line, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Deprecated (3.0): Returns (without removing) the earliest error code and optionally file, line, data text, and flags. Prefer ERR_peek_error_all.
requirements: Any of file, line, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.
Deprecated: avoid in new code.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the most recent error code on the calling thread’s queue. Returns 0 if none.
requirements: Non-destructive: does not pop.
Check for 0 to detect no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error_line
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the most recent error code and optionally its source file and line.
requirements: file and line may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error_func
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the most recent error code and optionally the function name associated with it.
requirements: func may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error_data
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the most recent error code and optionally the attached error data text and flags.
requirements: data and flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned data pointer refers to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error_all
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_peek_last_error_all(const char **file, int *line, const char **func, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the most recent error code and optionally retrieves file, line, function, data text, and flags.
requirements: Any of file, line, func, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_peek_last_error_line_data
functions.signature: unsigned long ERR_peek_last_error_line_data(const char **file, int *line, const char **data, int *flags);
functions.description: Deprecated (3.0): Returns (without removing) the most recent error code and optionally file, line, data text, and flags. Prefer ERR_peek_last_error_all.
requirements: Any of file, line, data, flags may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers refer to internal storage; copy if needed.
Check return value 0 for no error.
Thread-affine.
Deprecated: avoid in new code.

functions.name: ERR_clear_error
functions.description: Clears the calling thread’s entire OpenSSL error queue.
requirements: Thread-affine: clears only the calling thread’s queue.

functions.name: ERR_error_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the error code e. If buf is non-NULL, writes the string into buf (which must be large enough), otherwise returns a static buffer pointer.
requirements: If buf is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the full message (use ERR_error_string_n to avoid truncation).
Return may point to internal static storage if buf is NULL; copy if needed for thread safety or longevity.

functions.name: ERR_error_string_n
functions.signature: void ERR_error_string_n(unsigned long e, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable string for error code e into buf, truncated as needed to fit len bytes including the terminating NUL.
requirements: buf must be a valid writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be > 0 to receive a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: ERR_lib_error_string
functions.description: Returns a constant string naming the library component encoded in error code e, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to constant storage; do not modify or free.
e must be an OpenSSL-formatted error code.

functions.name: ERR_func_error_string
functions.description: Deprecated (3.0): Returns a constant string naming the function encoded in error code e, or NULL if unavailable. Function codes are not used in modern OpenSSL.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to constant storage; do not modify or free.
Deprecated: may return NULL or empty for modern codes; avoid in new code.

functions.name: ERR_reason_error_string
functions.description: Returns a constant string describing the reason portion of error code e, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to constant storage; do not modify or free.
e must be an OpenSSL-formatted error code or a system error code (for which mapping may be limited).

functions.name: ERR_print_errors_cb
functions.signature: void ERR_print_errors_cb(int (*cb)(const char *str, size_t len, void *u), void *u);
functions.description: Formats all errors on the calling thread’s error queue into human-readable lines and feeds each line to the user callback cb, passing u as user data. Consumes (clears) the queue as it prints.
requirements: cb must be a valid function pointer matching the required signature.
The callback must be reentrant-safe with respect to its own use of OpenSSL (if any).
Thread-affine: prints the calling thread’s queue and drains it.

functions.name: ERR_print_errors_fp
functions.description: Formats and writes the calling thread’s error queue to the given stdio FILE*, consuming the queue.
requirements: fp must be a valid, writable FILE* opened for output.
Unavailable if OpenSSL is built with OPENSSL_NO_STDIO.

functions.name: ERR_print_errors
functions.description: Formats and writes the calling thread’s error queue into the specified OpenSSL BIO, consuming the queue.
requirements: bp must be a valid, writable BIO* suitable for text output.

functions.name: ERR_add_error_data
functions.description: Appends additional text items to the most recent error’s data field by concatenating num string arguments in order.
requirements: num must be >= 1 and match the count of following variadic char* string arguments.
Each variadic argument should be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.
Must be called after an error is active (e.g., after ERR_new/ERR_set_error).
Thread-affine: operates on the calling thread’s current error.

functions.name: ERR_add_error_vdata
functions.description: va_list variant of ERR_add_error_data that appends num string items from args to the current error’s data.
requirements: num must be >= 1 and correspond to the number of strings in args.
args must be an initialized va_list whose elements are char* strings.
Must be called while an error is active.
va_list must be valid for the duration of the call.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_add_error_txt
functions.description: Appends text to the current error’s data, optionally inserting a separator string before the text.
requirements: txt should be a valid NUL-terminated string.
sepr, if provided, should be a valid NUL-terminated string; behavior when NULL is implementation-defined.
Must be called while an error is active.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_add_error_mem_bio
functions.description: Appends the contents of the given memory BIO to the current error’s data, optionally preceded by a separator string.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO that can be read to obtain its contents (typically a memory BIO).
sep, if provided, should be a valid NUL-terminated string; behavior when NULL is implementation-defined.
Must be called while an error is active.
Thread-affine.

functions.name: ERR_load_strings
functions.description: Registers a table of error strings for a specific library code, enabling human-readable mapping for error and reason codes.
requirements: lib must identify the library (e.g., ERR_LIB_*).
str must point to a valid ERR_STRING_DATA table; exact table termination and contents are not documented here (unknown).
Must be called during initialization before errors from that library are reported for readable output.

functions.name: ERR_load_strings_const
functions.description: Registers a constant table of error strings not tied to a specific lib id (or containing its own ids).
requirements: str must point to a valid, constant ERR_STRING_DATA table; exact table termination and contents are not documented here (unknown).
Intended for built-in static tables.

functions.name: ERR_unload_strings
functions.description: Unregisters previously loaded error strings for a library code.
requirements: lib must be the target library id whose strings were loaded.

functions.name: OSSL_ERR_STATE_save_to_mark

functions.name: OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore

functions.name: OSSL_ERR_STATE_free
