requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY containing a public key.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio_PUBKEY_ex
functions.signature: int PEM_write_bio_PUBKEY_ex(BIO *out, const EVP_PKEY *x, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq);
functions.description: Extended version of PEM_write_bio_PUBKEY that allows specifying library context and property query.
requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
libctx may be NULL; propq is optional.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio_PrivateKey_traditional
functions.signature: int PEM_write_bio_PrivateKey_traditional(BIO *bp, const EVP_PKEY *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const unsigned char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Writes a private key using the traditional (type-specific) PEM format (e.g., RSA PRIVATE KEY) to a BIO, optionally encrypting.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
If enc is non-NULL, either kstr/klen supply password data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid
functions.signature: int PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid(BIO *bp, const EVP_PKEY *x, int nid, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Writes a private key to a BIO in encrypted PKCS#8 format using the specified PBE algorithm NID.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
nid specifies the PBE algorithm NID.
Either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey
functions.signature: int PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey(BIO *bp, const EVP_PKEY *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Writes a private key to a BIO in PKCS#8 format, optionally encrypted with the specified cipher or password callback.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
If enc is non-NULL, either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_bio
functions.signature: int i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_bio(BIO *bp, const EVP_PKEY *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Serializes a private key to PKCS#8 and writes it to a BIO, optionally encrypting using the specified cipher or callback.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
If enc is non-NULL, either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid_bio
functions.signature: int i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid_bio(BIO *bp, const EVP_PKEY *x, int nid, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Serializes a private key to encrypted PKCS#8 using a PBE identified by nid and writes it to a BIO.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
nid selects the PBE algorithm.
Either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: d2i_PKCS8PrivateKey_bio
functions.description: Reads a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo (possibly encrypted) from a BIO and decodes it to an EVP_PKEY, using a password callback if needed.
requirements: bp must be a valid readable BIO.
x may be NULL or an existing EVP_PKEY**.
cb/u may be required for encrypted input.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_fp
functions.signature: int i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_fp(FILE *fp, const EVP_PKEY *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Serializes a private key to PKCS#8 and writes it to a FILE*, optionally encrypting with a cipher or callback.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
If enc is non-NULL, either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid_fp
functions.signature: int i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid_fp(FILE *fp, const EVP_PKEY *x, int nid, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Serializes a private key to encrypted PKCS#8 using a PBE identified by nid and writes it to a FILE*.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
nid selects the PBE algorithm.
Either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid
functions.signature: int PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid(FILE *fp, const EVP_PKEY *x, int nid, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Writes a private key to a FILE* in PKCS#8 format using the given PBE algorithm NID for encryption.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
nid selects the PBE algorithm.
Either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cb/u may be used.

functions.name: d2i_PKCS8PrivateKey_fp
functions.description: Reads a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo (possibly encrypted) from a FILE* and decodes it to an EVP_PKEY, using a password callback if needed.
requirements: fp must be a valid readable FILE*.
x may be NULL or an existing EVP_PKEY**.
cb/u may be required for encrypted input.

functions.name: PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey
functions.signature: int PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey(FILE *fp, const EVP_PKEY *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const char *kstr, int klen, pem_password_cb *cd, void *u);
functions.description: Writes a private key to a FILE* in PKCS#8 format, optionally encrypting with the specified cipher or password callback.
requirements: fp must be a valid writable FILE*.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
If enc is non-NULL, either kstr/klen supply passphrase data or cd/u may be used.

functions.name: PEM_read_bio_Parameters_ex
functions.description: Reads domain parameters (e.g., for DH/DSA/EC) from a BIO in PEM format into an EVP_PKEY, with library context and property query.
requirements: bp must be a valid readable BIO.
x may be NULL or an existing EVP_PKEY**.
libctx may be NULL; propq is optional.

functions.name: PEM_read_bio_Parameters
functions.description: Reads domain parameters (e.g., for DH/DSA/EC) from a BIO in PEM format into an EVP_PKEY.
requirements: bp must be a valid readable BIO.
x may be NULL or an existing EVP_PKEY**.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio_Parameters
functions.description: Writes domain parameters (e.g., for DH/DSA/EC) from an EVP_PKEY to a BIO in PEM format.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
x must be a valid EVP_PKEY containing parameters.

functions.name: b2i_PrivateKey
functions.description: Decodes a private key from a specific binary (non-PEM) format in memory to an EVP_PKEY.
requirements: in must point to a pointer to the beginning of the input buffer; it may be advanced by the function.
length must be the number of bytes available at *in and must be non-negative.

functions.name: b2i_PublicKey
functions.description: Decodes a public key from a specific binary (non-PEM) format in memory to an EVP_PKEY.
requirements: in must point to the input buffer pointer; it may be advanced by the function.
length must be the size of the buffer in bytes and non-negative.

functions.name: b2i_PrivateKey_bio
functions.description: Decodes a private key from a specific binary (non-PEM) format read from a BIO to an EVP_PKEY.
requirements: in must be a valid readable BIO positioned at the key data.

functions.name: b2i_PublicKey_bio
functions.description: Decodes a public key from a specific binary (non-PEM) format read from a BIO to an EVP_PKEY.
requirements: in must be a valid readable BIO.

functions.name: i2b_PrivateKey_bio
functions.description: Encodes a private key to a specific binary (non-PEM) format and writes it to a BIO.
requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
pk must be a valid EVP_PKEY with a private key.

functions.name: i2b_PublicKey_bio
functions.description: Encodes a public key to a specific binary (non-PEM) format and writes it to a BIO.
requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
pk must be a valid EVP_PKEY with a public key.

functions.name: b2i_PVK_bio
functions.description: Decodes a Microsoft PVK format key from a BIO to an EVP_PKEY, using a password callback if the PVK is encrypted.
requirements: in must be a valid readable BIO.
cb/u may be required if the PVK is password-protected.

functions.name: b2i_PVK_bio_ex
functions.signature: EVP_PKEY *b2i_PVK_bio_ex(BIO *in, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq);
functions.description: Extended variant of PVK decoding with library context and property query for algorithm fetching.
requirements: in must be a valid readable BIO.
cb/u may be required for encrypted PVK files.
libctx may be NULL; propq is optional.

functions.name: i2b_PVK_bio
functions.signature: int i2b_PVK_bio(BIO *out, const EVP_PKEY *pk, int enclevel, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Encodes an EVP_PKEY into Microsoft PVK format and writes it to a BIO, optionally encrypting based on enclevel and callback.
requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
pk must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
enclevel controls encryption level for PVK output.
cb/u may be used to obtain a password when encryption is requested.

functions.name: i2b_PVK_bio_ex
functions.signature: int i2b_PVK_bio_ex(BIO *out, const EVP_PKEY *pk, int enclevel, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq);
functions.description: Extended variant of PVK encoding with library context and property query, optionally encrypting based on enclevel and callback.
requirements: out must be a valid writable BIO.
pk must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
enclevel controls encryption level.
cb/u may be used for password input.
libctx may be NULL; propq is optional.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_options
functions.description: Returns the options bitmask currently active on the given SSL_CTX. Typical usage is to inspect which SSL_OP_* flags are set for a context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_get_options
functions.description: Returns the options bitmask currently active on the given SSL connection object. Typical usage is to inspect which SSL_OP_* flags are set for a connection.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_clear_options
functions.description: Clears (unsets) the specified SSL_OP_* option flags in an SSL_CTX, returning the new options bitmask.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX pointer.
op is a bitmask of SSL_OP_* flags to clear.

functions.name: SSL_clear_options
functions.description: Clears (unsets) the specified SSL_OP_* option flags on an SSL connection, returning the new options bitmask.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL* pointer.
op is a bitmask of SSL_OP_* flags to clear.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_options
functions.description: Sets (ORs in) the specified SSL_OP_* option flags on an SSL_CTX, returning the new options bitmask. Note: setting uses |= semantics; use SSL_CTX_clear_options to unset.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX pointer.
op is a bitmask of SSL_OP_* flags to set.

functions.name: SSL_set_options
functions.description: Sets (ORs in) the specified SSL_OP_* option flags on an SSL connection, returning the new options bitmask. Note: setting uses |= semantics; use SSL_clear_options to unset.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL* pointer.
op is a bitmask of SSL_OP_* flags to set.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_ctrl
functions.signature: long SSL_CTX_ctrl(SSL_CTX *ctx, int cmd, long larg, void *parg);
functions.description: Generic control interface for SSL_CTX. Performs a command specified by cmd (e.g., SSL_CTRL_* constants), with numeric parameter larg and pointer parameter parg. Many SSL_CTX_* convenience macros are wrappers over this.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX pointer.
cmd must be a supported SSL_CTRL_* (or related DTLS/TLS) control command for contexts.
The meaning and validity of larg and parg depend on cmd; caller must provide appropriate argument types per command’s contract.
Return value semantics depend on cmd (often >0 for success, 0/<=0 for failure).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_mode
functions.signature: long SSL_CTX_get_mode(SSL_CTX *ctx) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_CTX_ctrl(ctx, SSL_CTRL_MODE, 0, NULL) */
functions.description: Returns the current SSL mode bitmask configured on an SSL_CTX. This is a function-like macro that forwards to SSL_CTX_ctrl. Typical usage is to inspect flags like SSL_MODE_AUTO_RETRY, etc.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX pointer

functions.name: SSL_clear_mode
functions.signature: long SSL_clear_mode(SSL *ssl, long op) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, SSL_CTRL_CLEAR_MODE, op, NULL) */
functions.description: Clears the specified mode bits on an SSL object. This is a function-like macro that forwards to SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
op must be a bitmask composed of SSL_MODE_* flags

functions.name: SSL_set_mode
functions.signature: long SSL_set_mode(SSL *ssl, long op) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, SSL_CTRL_MODE, op, NULL) */
functions.description: Sets (ORs in) the specified mode bits on an SSL object. This is a function-like macro that forwards to SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
op must be a bitmask composed of SSL_MODE_* flags

functions.name: SSL_get_mode
functions.signature: long SSL_get_mode(SSL *ssl) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, SSL_CTRL_MODE, 0, NULL) */
functions.description: Returns the current mode bitmask configured on an SSL object. This is a function-like macro that forwards to SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_ctrl
functions.signature: long SSL_ctrl(SSL *ssl, int cmd, long larg, void *parg);
functions.description: Generic control interface for SSL connections. Performs a command specified by cmd (e.g., SSL_CTRL_* or DTLS_CTRL_*), with numeric parameter larg and pointer parameter parg. Many SSL_* convenience macros are wrappers over this.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, initialized SSL* pointer.
cmd must be a supported SSL_CTRL_* or DTLS_CTRL_* command for connections.
The meaning and validity of larg and parg depend on cmd; caller must supply correct argument types for the chosen command.
Return value semantics depend on cmd (often >0 for success, 0/<=0 for failure).

functions.name: DTLS_set_link_mtu
functions.signature: long DTLS_set_link_mtu(SSL *ssl, long mtu) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, DTLS_CTRL_SET_LINK_MTU, mtu, NULL) */
functions.description: Sets the link-layer MTU for a DTLS connection. This influences DTLS record sizing. Function-like macro wrapper around SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, DTLS-based SSL pointer
mtu should be a positive integer representing the link MTU; exact acceptable ranges are implementation-defined

functions.name: DTLS_get_link_min_mtu
functions.signature: long DTLS_get_link_min_mtu(SSL *ssl) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, DTLS_CTRL_GET_LINK_MIN_MTU, 0, NULL) */
functions.description: Returns the minimum viable link MTU for the DTLS connection, as determined by the library. Function-like macro wrapper around SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, DTLS-based SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_secure_renegotiation_support
functions.signature: long SSL_get_secure_renegotiation_support(SSL *ssl) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(ssl, SSL_CTRL_GET_RI_SUPPORT, 0, NULL) */
functions.description: Reports whether RFC 5746 secure renegotiation is supported/negotiated. Returns nonzero if supported. Function-like macro wrapper around SSL_ctrl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_set_cert_flags
functions.signature: long SSL_set_cert_flags(SSL *s, long op) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(s, SSL_CTRL_CERT_FLAGS, op, NULL) */
functions.description: Sets (ORs in) certificate-handling flags on an SSL object (e.g., SSL_CERT_FLAG_TLS_STRICT). Function-like macro wrapper around SSL_ctrl.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
op must be a bitmask of SSL_CERT_FLAG_* values

functions.name: SSL_clear_cert_flags
functions.signature: long SSL_clear_cert_flags(SSL *s, long op) /* function-like macro mapping to SSL_ctrl(s, SSL_CTRL_CLEAR_CERT_FLAGS, op, NULL) */
functions.description: Clears specified certificate-handling flags on an SSL object. Function-like macro wrapper around SSL_ctrl.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
op must be a bitmask of SSL_CERT_FLAG_* values

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_msg_callback
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_set_msg_callback(SSL_CTX *ctx, void (*cb)(int write_p, int version, int content_type, const void *buf, size_t len, SSL *ssl, void *arg));
functions.description: Registers a per-context message callback invoked for each SSL/TLS record sent or received. The callback observes protocol version, content type, and raw record bytes. Intended for debugging/tracing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable the callback; if non-NULL, it must be callable for the lifetime of ctx or until replaced.
The callback must not modify internal SSL buffers referenced by buf and must return promptly (no long blocking).
Use SSL_CTX_set_msg_callback_arg (macro via SSL_CTX_ctrl) to set the user arg accessible in the callback.

functions.name: SSL_set_msg_callback
functions.signature: void SSL_set_msg_callback(SSL *ssl, void (*cb)(int write_p, int version, int content_type, const void *buf, size_t len, SSL *ssl, void *arg));
functions.description: Registers a per-connection message callback, invoked for each SSL/TLS record sent or received on this SSL object. Overrides any context-level callback for this connection.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable the callback; if non-NULL, it must remain valid for the life of ssl or until replaced.
The callback must not modify internal SSL buffers referenced by buf and should avoid long blocking.
Use SSL_set_msg_callback_arg (macro via SSL_ctrl) to set the user arg accessible in the callback.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_set_new_cb
functions.description: Sets a callback invoked when a new session is established and added to the session cache. Useful for tracking or persisting sessions.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
new_session_cb may be NULL to disable; if non-NULL, it must be callable whenever handshakes complete on connections using this ctx.

The callback should return nonzero to proceed and zero on error, as per OpenSSL convention for similar callbacks (note: exact return semantics for this specific callback are not described here; consult OpenSSL docs).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_get_new_cb
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured 'new session' callback for the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_set_remove_cb
functions.description: Sets a callback invoked when a session is removed from the internal session cache.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
remove_session_cb may be NULL to disable; if non-NULL it must be callable during session removal events.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_get_remove_cb
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured 'remove session' callback for the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_set_get_cb
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_sess_set_get_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx, SSL_SESSION *(*get_session_cb)(struct ssl_st *ssl, const unsigned char *data, int len, int *copy));
functions.description: Sets a callback to look up a session by ID when processing client session resumption. The callback should return an SSL_SESSION* or NULL if not found. If returning a session, it must set *copy to 1 if the library should up-ref, or 0 if the session is owned by the callback and will remain valid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
get_session_cb may be NULL to disable external lookup.
The callback must correctly manage ownership via the *copy out-parameter.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_sess_get_get_cb
functions.signature: SSL_SESSION *(*SSL_CTX_sess_get_get_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx))(struct ssl_st *ssl, const unsigned char *data, int len, int *copy);
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured external session lookup callback for the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_info_callback
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_set_info_callback(SSL_CTX *ctx, void (*cb)(const SSL *ssl, int type, int val));
functions.description: Sets a context-wide info callback invoked for various state changes and alerts during handshakes and I/O. Useful for tracing state machine progress.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable; if non-NULL, it must be callable whenever events occur on any SSL created from ctx.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_info_callback
functions.signature: void (*SSL_CTX_get_info_callback(SSL_CTX *ctx))(const SSL *ssl, int type, int val);
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured info callback for the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_client_cert_cb
functions.description: Sets the client-certificate selection callback for client authentication. The callback should set *x509 and *pkey to the certificate and private key to use and return 1 on success, 0 on failure, or -1 to suspend and resume later (typical OpenSSL semantics; exact values not stated in this header).
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
client_cert_cb may be NULL to disable.
The callback must set outputs (*x509, *pkey) appropriately when returning success and ensure they remain valid for use by the library.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_client_cert_cb
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured client-certificate selection callback for the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_cookie_generate_cb
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_set_cookie_generate_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx, int (*app_gen_cookie_cb)(SSL *ssl, unsigned char *cookie, unsigned int *cookie_len));
functions.description: Sets DTLS cookie generation callback (server side). The callback writes a cookie into buffer and sets cookie_len, returning 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
app_gen_cookie_cb may be NULL to disable.
cookie buffer and cookie_len pointers are provided by OpenSSL when invoking the callback; callback must not exceed provided buffer capacity (not specified here).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_cookie_verify_cb
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_set_cookie_verify_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx, int (*app_verify_cookie_cb)(SSL *ssl, const unsigned char *cookie, unsigned int cookie_len));
functions.description: Sets DTLS cookie verification callback (server side). The callback should return 1 if the cookie is valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
app_verify_cookie_cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb
functions.description: Sets the TLSv1.3 stateless cookie generation callback. The callback writes a cookie and sets its length. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (typical).
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
gen_stateless_cookie_cb may be NULL to disable.
OpenSSL supplies buffer and length pointer; callback must ensure bounds.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_stateless_cookie_verify_cb
functions.signature: void SSL_CTX_set_stateless_cookie_verify_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx, int (*verify_stateless_cookie_cb)(SSL *ssl, const unsigned char *cookie, size_t cookie_len));
functions.description: Sets the TLSv1.3 stateless cookie verification callback. Return 1 to accept the cookie, 0 to reject.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
verify_stateless_cookie_cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_next_protos_advertised_cb
functions.description: Sets the NPN (Next Protocol Negotiation) server-side callback to advertise supported protocols. The callback sets out/outlen to a wire-format protocol list.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
NPN is deprecated in favor of ALPN; only enable if needed for legacy interop.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_next_proto_select_cb
functions.description: Sets the NPN client-side selection callback. The callback selects a protocol from the server-provided list and sets out/outlen.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
NPN is deprecated in favor of ALPN.

functions.name: SSL_get0_next_proto_negotiated
functions.signature: void SSL_get0_next_proto_negotiated(const SSL *s, const unsigned char **data, unsigned *len);
functions.description: Retrieves the NPN-negotiated protocol for a connection. On return, *data points to internal memory containing the protocol string, and *len is its length. Data is valid while s is valid.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.
data and len must be non-NULL pointers if negotiation info is desired.

functions.name: SSL_select_next_proto
functions.signature: int SSL_select_next_proto(unsigned char **out, unsigned char *outlen, const unsigned char *server, unsigned int server_len, const unsigned char *client, unsigned int client_len);
functions.description: Implements NPN protocol selection: chooses the first client protocol that appears in the server list. On success sets *out/*outlen to point within server list; returns OPENSSL_NPN_NEGOTIATED or OPENSSL_NPN_NO_OVERLAP as appropriate.
requirements: out and outlen must be non-NULL.
server/server_len and client/client_len must point to valid, correctly formatted NPN protocol lists (length-prefixed).
No ownership transfer; returned pointer aliases server buffer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_alpn_protos
functions.signature: int SSL_CTX_set_alpn_protos(SSL_CTX *ctx, const unsigned char *protos, unsigned int protos_len);
functions.description: Sets ALPN protocol list on an SSL_CTX for client use. The list is in wire format: a sequence of 8-bit length-prefixed strings. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
protos points to a buffer containing properly formatted ALPN protocol list; protos_len is its size.

functions.name: SSL_set_alpn_protos
functions.signature: int SSL_set_alpn_protos(SSL *ssl, const unsigned char *protos, unsigned int protos_len);
functions.description: Sets ALPN protocol list on a single SSL connection for client use. Wire-format as for SSL_CTX_set_alpn_protos. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* pointer.
protos must be a valid ALPN list buffer; protos_len its size.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_alpn_select_cb
functions.description: Sets the ALPN server-side selection callback. The callback selects a protocol based on the client's offered list.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
Callback must set *out/*outlen to a protocol string owned by OpenSSL or to a stable buffer for the duration of the handshake.

functions.name: SSL_get0_alpn_selected
functions.signature: void SSL_get0_alpn_selected(const SSL *ssl, const unsigned char **data, unsigned int *len);
functions.description: Retrieves the ALPN-negotiated protocol for a connection. *data points to internal storage valid while ssl is valid; *len receives length.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* pointer.
data and len must be non-NULL to receive values.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_psk_client_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy PSK client callback for TLS <=1.2. The callback fills identity and psk buffers and returns the PSK length on success, or 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
Identity and PSK buffers provided at call time have maximum sizes PSK_MAX_IDENTITY_LEN and PSK_MAX_PSK_LEN.

functions.name: SSL_set_psk_client_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy PSK client callback on a per-connection basis. See SSL_CTX_set_psk_client_callback.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_psk_server_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy PSK server callback for TLS <=1.2. The callback receives the client identity and must write the PSK into the buffer, returning its length on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
PSK buffer length is limited to PSK_MAX_PSK_LEN.

functions.name: SSL_set_psk_server_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy PSK server callback on a per-connection basis. See SSL_CTX_set_psk_server_callback.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_psk_identity_hint
functions.description: Sets a server-side PSK identity hint at the context level (TLS <=1.2). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
identity_hint may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL, must be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: SSL_use_psk_identity_hint
functions.description: Sets a server-side PSK identity hint on a single connection (TLS <=1.2). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.
identity_hint may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL, must be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: SSL_get_psk_identity_hint
functions.description: Returns the configured server-side PSK identity hint for the connection, or NULL if none. The returned pointer is owned by OpenSSL and valid while s is valid.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_get_psk_identity
functions.description: Returns the client PSK identity used/selected for the connection, or NULL if none. The returned pointer is owned by OpenSSL and valid while s is valid.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_set_psk_find_session_callback
functions.description: Registers a TLS 1.3 PSK find-session callback for a specific connection. The callback looks up a resumption or external PSK by identity and returns a session via output parameters.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
Callback must set output SSL_SESSION** appropriately and follow ownership rules documented by OpenSSL.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_psk_find_session_callback
functions.description: Registers a TLS 1.3 PSK find-session callback at the context level. See SSL_set_psk_find_session_callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_set_psk_use_session_callback
functions.description: Registers a TLS 1.3 client callback to supply a PSK session to use (and associated identity).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.
Callback must set outputs (id, idlen, sess) correctly; ownership/refs as per OpenSSL docs.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_psk_use_session_callback
functions.description: Registers a TLS 1.3 client PSK use-session callback at the context level. See SSL_set_psk_use_session_callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_has_client_custom_ext
functions.signature: int SSL_CTX_has_client_custom_ext(const SSL_CTX *ctx, unsigned int ext_type);
functions.description: Checks whether a client custom TLS extension handler is registered for the given extension type in this SSL_CTX. Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
ext_type is a numeric TLS extension type code.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add_client_custom_ext
functions.signature: int SSL_CTX_add_client_custom_ext(SSL_CTX *ctx, unsigned int ext_type, custom_ext_add_cb add_cb, custom_ext_free_cb free_cb, void *add_arg, custom_ext_parse_cb parse_cb, void *parse_arg);
functions.description: Registers client-side custom extension add/free/parse callbacks for the given extension type. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
ext_type must be an unsigned extension type number not already registered.
add_cb and parse_cb define behavior for sending and parsing; free_cb may be NULL if not needed.
Callback arguments add_arg/parse_arg are passed back to the respective callbacks.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add_server_custom_ext
functions.signature: int SSL_CTX_add_server_custom_ext(SSL_CTX *ctx, unsigned int ext_type, custom_ext_add_cb add_cb, custom_ext_free_cb free_cb, void *add_arg, custom_ext_parse_cb parse_cb, void *parse_arg);
functions.description: Registers server-side custom extension add/free/parse callbacks for the given extension type. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
ext_type must be a valid extension type number not already registered for server role.
Callbacks and args as per client-side variant.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext
functions.signature: int SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext(SSL_CTX *ctx, unsigned int ext_type, unsigned int context, SSL_custom_ext_add_cb_ex add_cb, SSL_custom_ext_free_cb_ex free_cb, void *add_arg, SSL_custom_ext_parse_cb_ex parse_cb, void *parse_arg);
functions.description: Registers rich custom TLS extension callbacks (with TLS 1.3 contexts and certificate chain index info) for client and/or server, as indicated by 'context'. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
ext_type is the numeric extension type code.
context is a bitmask of SSL_EXT_* context codes appropriate for where the extension is valid.
add_cb/parse_cb define sending and parsing; free_cb may be NULL.
add_arg/parse_arg are opaque user pointers passed to callbacks.

functions.name: SSL_extension_supported
functions.description: Reports whether the library implements support for the given TLS extension type. Returns 1 if supported, 0 otherwise.
requirements: ext_type is a numeric TLS extension type code.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_keylog_callback
functions.description: Sets a callback to log TLS key material (for debugging with tools like Wireshark). The callback is invoked with a single text line to log.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cb may be NULL to disable; if non-NULL, it must be safe for concurrent use and should append a newline after logging line, per convention.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_keylog_callback
functions.description: Returns the currently configured keylog callback for the SSL_CTX (or NULL if none).
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_max_early_data
functions.description: Configures the maximum amount of TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT) the server will accept (or client will advertise). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_max_early_data
functions.description: Returns the configured maximum early data size on the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_set_max_early_data
functions.description: Sets the per-connection maximum early data size (overrides context). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_get_max_early_data
functions.description: Returns the per-connection maximum early data size.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_recv_max_early_data
functions.description: Sets the maximum amount of early data the server will actually receive/process. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_recv_max_early_data
functions.description: Returns the configured maximum early data receive limit on the SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: SSL_set_recv_max_early_data
functions.description: Sets the per-connection limit on early data the server will receive/process. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: SSL_get_recv_max_early_data
functions.description: Returns the per-connection early data receive limit.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL* pointer.

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_num
functions.description: Returns the number of elements in a STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER). Wrapper macro over the generic OPENSSL stack API.
requirements: sk may be NULL; if NULL the behavior follows OPENSSL_sk_num (commonly returns 0)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_value
functions.description: Returns the element at position idx from a STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER). Wrapper macro over OPENSSL_sk_value.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
idx must be in the range [0, sk_SSL_CIPHER_num(sk) - 1]

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_new
functions.description: Creates a new empty STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) with an optional comparison function for ordering.
requirements: cmp may be NULL (unsorted) or a valid comparator compatible with OPENSSL_sk_new

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_new_null
functions.description: Creates a new empty STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) without a comparison function.

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_new_reserve
functions.signature: STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) *sk_SSL_CIPHER_new_reserve(int (*cmp)(const SSL_CIPHER *, const SSL_CIPHER *), int n)
functions.description: Creates a new STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) with an optional comparison function and reserves capacity for n elements.
requirements: n should be non-negative; actual limits are implementation-defined

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_reserve
functions.description: Ensures the stack has capacity for at least n elements. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
n should be non-negative

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_free
functions.description: Frees a STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) structure (but not the SSL_CIPHER elements unless owned by the stack via other APIs).
requirements: sk may be NULL (no effect)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_zero
functions.description: Removes all elements from the stack without freeing the stack itself.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_delete
functions.description: Deletes and returns the element at index i from the stack.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
i must be within valid index range

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_delete_ptr
functions.description: Deletes the first matching element equal to ptr from the stack and returns it.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
ptr must be a pointer to an element currently present in the stack or NULL (no-op)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_push
functions.description: Appends ptr to the end of the stack. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
ptr may be NULL depending on application semantics; the stack stores the pointer as-is

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_unshift
functions.description: Inserts ptr at the beginning of the stack. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the last element of the stack, or NULL if empty.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_shift
functions.description: Removes and returns the first element of the stack, or NULL if empty.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_pop_free
functions.description: Pops all elements from the stack and frees each element using freefunc, then frees the stack.
requirements: sk may be NULL (no effect)
freefunc must be a valid function pointer compatible with freeing SSL_CIPHER elements

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_insert
functions.signature: int sk_SSL_CIPHER_insert(STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) *sk, const SSL_CIPHER *ptr, int idx)
functions.description: Inserts ptr at position idx in the stack. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
idx must be within or just past the end of the current range (implementation-defined for bounds)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_set
functions.signature: const SSL_CIPHER *sk_SSL_CIPHER_set(STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) *sk, int idx, const SSL_CIPHER *ptr)
functions.description: Replaces the element at idx with ptr, returning the previous element pointer.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
idx must be in range [0, sk_SSL_CIPHER_num(sk)-1]

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_find
functions.description: Finds the index of ptr in the sorted stack using the comparison function; returns index or -1 if not found.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) (typically sorted if relying on binary search semantics)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_find_ex
functions.description: Like sk_SSL_CIPHER_find but with extended semantics consistent with OPENSSL_sk_find_ex (e.g., insertion point); returns index or negative on not found per OPENSSL rules.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) (typically sorted)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_find_all
functions.signature: int sk_SSL_CIPHER_find_all(const STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) *sk, const SSL_CIPHER *ptr, size_t *pnum)
functions.description: Finds all indices matching ptr according to the comparator and writes the number of matches to pnum. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
pnum must be a valid pointer to size_t for receiving the count

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_sort
functions.description: Sorts the stack using its comparator.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
A comparator must have been set or default semantics apply

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_is_sorted
functions.description: Returns 1 if the stack is known to be sorted, 0 otherwise.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_dup
functions.description: Creates a shallow duplicate of the stack (elements are not deep-copied).
requirements: sk may be NULL (returns NULL)

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_deep_copy
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of the stack using copyfunc for each element and freefunc to free on failure.
requirements: sk may be NULL (returns NULL)
copyfunc and freefunc must be valid if deep-copying is desired

functions.name: sk_SSL_CIPHER_set_cmp_func
functions.signature: int (*sk_SSL_CIPHER_set_cmp_func(STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER) *sk, int (*cmp)(const SSL_CIPHER *, const SSL_CIPHER *)))(const SSL_CIPHER *, const SSL_CIPHER *)
functions.description: Sets the comparison function for the stack and returns the previous comparator.
requirements: sk must be a valid STACK_OF(SSL_CIPHER)
cmp may be NULL to clear comparator or a valid comparator function

functions.name: SSL_in_init
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the SSL object is in the process of performing the handshake (initialization).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_in_before
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the SSL object is in the 'before' state (no handshake initiated yet).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_is_init_finished
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the handshake has completed successfully and the connection is ready for application data.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_finished
functions.signature: size_t SSL_get_finished(const SSL *s, void *buf, size_t count)
functions.description: Obtains the latest Finished message we sent. Returns its length and copies up to count bytes into buf.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
If count > 0, buf must point to a writable buffer of at least count bytes

functions.name: SSL_get_peer_finished
functions.signature: size_t SSL_get_peer_finished(const SSL *s, void *buf, size_t count)
functions.description: Obtains the latest Finished message we expected from the peer. Returns its length and copies up to count bytes into buf.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
If count > 0, buf must point to a writable buffer of at least count bytes

functions.name: SSL_get_current_cipher
functions.description: Returns the currently active cipher for the connection, or NULL if not negotiated.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_pending_cipher
functions.description: Returns the cipher that is pending to become active (e.g., after a renegotiation) or NULL if none.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_bits
functions.description: Returns the number of secret bits of the cipher; optionally stores algorithm bits in alg_bits.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer
alg_bits may be NULL or a valid int pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_version
functions.description: Returns a human-readable protocol version string associated with the cipher (e.g., "TLSv1.2").
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_name
functions.description: Returns the library's short name for the cipher (e.g., "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256").
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_standard_name
functions.description: Returns the IANA standard name for the cipher, if available, else NULL or an alias.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: OPENSSL_cipher_name
functions.description: Maps an RFC/IANA cipher suite name to the OpenSSL internal name, if available. Useful for name conversions.
requirements: rfc_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated string

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_id
functions.description: Returns the internal 32-bit cipher identifier.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_protocol_id
functions.description: Returns the IANA-assigned 16-bit cipher protocol ID.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_kx_nid
functions.description: Returns the NID for the key exchange algorithm of the cipher, or NID_undef if not applicable.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_auth_nid
functions.description: Returns the NID for the authentication algorithm of the cipher, or NID_undef if not applicable.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_get_handshake_digest
functions.description: Returns the message digest used in the handshake for the given cipher, or NULL if not applicable.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_CIPHER_is_aead
functions.description: Returns 1 if the cipher is an AEAD cipher (e.g., GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305), 0 otherwise.
requirements: c must be a valid SSL_CIPHER pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor associated with the SSL's underlying I/O BIO for both read and write if it is a socket BIO. If no socket-based BIO is present, returns -1. Useful to integrate SSL with poll/select or to query the underlying socket.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
Returns -1 if no file descriptor is available (e.g., non-socket BIOs)

functions.name: SSL_get_rfd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor used for reading for the SSL's underlying read BIO if it is a socket BIO. Returns -1 if not applicable.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
May return -1 if the read BIO is not a socket BIO or is unset

functions.name: SSL_get_wfd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor used for writing for the SSL's underlying write BIO if it is a socket BIO. Returns -1 if not applicable.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized SSL pointer
May return -1 if the write BIO is not a socket BIO or is unset

functions.name: SSL_get_cipher_list
functions.description: Returns the name of the n-th configured cipher in the client's or server's cipher list for the SSL object. Use sequential n starting at 0 to enumerate.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
n must be >= 0 and within the list bounds; returns NULL if out of range

functions.name: SSL_get_shared_ciphers
functions.description: Writes a colon-separated string of ciphers shared between client and server into buf. Returns buf on success or NULL on failure/insufficient buffer.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer with negotiated/shared ciphers available
buf must be non-NULL with capacity >= 1; size specifies buffer length in bytes
If size is too small, function may fail and return NULL

functions.name: SSL_get_read_ahead
functions.description: Returns the current read-ahead setting for the SSL object (non-zero if enabled). Read-ahead controls whether the record layer reads more data than requested.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_pending
functions.description: Returns the number of application bytes which have been processed internally and can be read immediately from SSL_read without blocking.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
The value is advisory and pertains to decrypted, buffered data

functions.name: SSL_has_pending
functions.description: Returns 1 if there is any pending data (application or other) inside the SSL/TLS record layer for immediate processing; 0 otherwise.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_set_fd
functions.description: Associates a socket file descriptor fd with both the read and write sides of the SSL object using socket BIOs.
requirements: Available only when OpenSSL is built without OPENSSL_NO_SOCK
s must be a valid, newly created or cleared SSL object
fd must be a valid OS socket descriptor opened in a mode compatible with the desired I/O (blocking/nonblocking)
On success, the SSL owns the BIOs tied to fd; do not separately free them

functions.name: SSL_set_rfd
functions.description: Associates a socket file descriptor fd as the read BIO for the SSL object.
requirements: Available only when OpenSSL is built without OPENSSL_NO_SOCK
s must be a valid SSL object
fd must be a valid socket descriptor
Sets/updates only the read side; write side remains unchanged

functions.name: SSL_set_wfd
functions.description: Associates a socket file descriptor fd as the write BIO for the SSL object.
requirements: Available only when OpenSSL is built without OPENSSL_NO_SOCK
s must be a valid SSL object
fd must be a valid socket descriptor
Sets/updates only the write side; read side remains unchanged

functions.name: SSL_set0_rbio
functions.description: Sets the read BIO for the SSL object to rbio without incrementing its reference; ownership is transferred to SSL (SSL will free it).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL object
rbio may be NULL to clear the read BIO
Caller must not free rbio after this call (ownership transferred)

functions.name: SSL_set0_wbio
functions.description: Sets the write BIO for the SSL object to wbio without incrementing its reference; ownership is transferred to SSL (SSL will free it).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL object
wbio may be NULL to clear the write BIO
Caller must not free wbio after this call (ownership transferred)

functions.name: SSL_set_bio
functions.description: Sets both the read and write BIOs for the SSL object. Ownership of the passed BIOs is transferred to SSL (they will be freed by SSL).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL object
rbio and/or wbio may be NULL to clear sides
Do not free rbio/wbio after calling; ownership is transferred

functions.name: SSL_get_rbio
functions.description: Returns the current read BIO associated with the SSL object, or NULL if none.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
Returned BIO remains owned by SSL; do not free it

functions.name: SSL_get_wbio
functions.description: Returns the current write BIO associated with the SSL object, or NULL if none.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
Returned BIO remains owned by SSL; do not free it

functions.name: SSL_set_cipher_list
functions.description: Configures the list and order of ciphers for TLS 1.2 and below on a single SSL object using OpenSSL's cipher string syntax (e.g., "DEFAULT:!aNULL").
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
str must be non-NULL and follow OpenSSL cipher list syntax
A successful return indicates at least one cipher matched; returns 0 if no ciphers matched or on error

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_ciphersuites
functions.description: Sets the enabled TLSv1.3 ciphersuites for an SSL_CTX using IANA names in a colon-separated list.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer
str must be non-NULL and contain valid TLSv1.3 ciphersuite names
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (e.g., no valid suites parsed)

functions.name: SSL_set_ciphersuites
functions.description: Sets the enabled TLSv1.3 ciphersuites for a specific SSL using IANA names in a colon-separated list.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
str must be non-NULL and contain valid TLSv1.3 ciphersuite names
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error

functions.name: SSL_set_read_ahead
functions.description: Enables or disables read-ahead for the SSL object. When enabled (non-zero), the record layer may read more bytes than requested.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_verify_mode
functions.description: Returns the current peer verification mode flags for the SSL object (e.g., SSL_VERIFY_NONE, SSL_VERIFY_PEER, etc.).
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_verify_depth
functions.description: Returns the maximum certificate chain verification depth set on the SSL object, or -1 if unset/default.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_get_verify_callback
functions.description: Returns the application-defined verification callback set with SSL_set_verify for this SSL object, or NULL if none.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer

functions.name: SSL_set_verify
functions.signature: void SSL_set_verify(SSL *s, int mode, SSL_verify_cb callback);
functions.description: Sets peer verification mode and optional verification callback for the SSL object. The callback is invoked during X.509 verification.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
mode should be a combination of SSL_VERIFY_* flags
callback may be NULL to use default verification behavior

functions.name: SSL_set_verify_depth
functions.description: Sets maximum verification chain depth for peer certificate validation on the SSL object.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
depth must be >= 0

functions.name: SSL_set_cert_cb
functions.description: Registers a certificate callback invoked by the handshake when certificate/private key material is needed. The callback can supply or defer credentials.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer
cb may be NULL to clear the callback
cb should return values as documented by OpenSSL (e.g., 1 success, 0/negative to indicate retry/error)

functions.name: SSL_use_PrivateKey
functions.description: Sets the private key for the SSL connection from an EVP_PKEY object.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer
pkey must be a valid EVP_PKEY matching the configured certificate (if any)
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (check error stack)

functions.name: SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1
functions.signature: int SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1(int pk, SSL *ssl, const unsigned char *d, long len);
functions.description: Loads a private key for the SSL connection from ASN.1 (DER) encoded bytes of type pk.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer
d must point to DER-encoded key data of length len
pk specifies the key type (EVP_PKEY type id)
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error

functions.name: SSL_use_certificate
functions.description: Sets the leaf certificate for the SSL connection from an X509 object.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer
x must be a valid X509 certificate
Certificate should be appropriate for the connection role (server/client)
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error

functions.name: SSL_use_certificate_ASN1

functions.name: RAND_bytes_ex

requirements: If ctx is NULL, the default library context is used.
