functions.description: Returns the short name (sn) string for a given NID.
requirements: n must be a valid NID.
Caller must check for NULL return if the NID has no short name.
Returned pointer is not to be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: OBJ_obj2nid
functions.description: Maps an ASN1_OBJECT to its corresponding NID value.
requirements: o must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT.
Return value should be checked; unknown objects may map to NID_undef (typically 0) though this is not stated here.

functions.name: OBJ_txt2obj
functions.description: Parses a text representation of an object identifier into an ASN1_OBJECT. The text can be a dotted numeric OID or (depending on no_name) a short/long name.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string containing either a dotted OID or a known name.
If no_name is nonzero, only dotted numeric OIDs are accepted; if zero, names may be accepted (behavior inferred from conventional OpenSSL usage).
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned ASN1_OBJECT is not specified here; caller should treat it as allocated and free with appropriate API if documented elsewhere.

functions.name: OBJ_obj2txt
functions.signature: int OBJ_obj2txt(char *buf, int buf_len, const ASN1_OBJECT *a, int no_name);
functions.description: Converts an ASN1_OBJECT to its text form (name or dotted OID) and writes it into the provided buffer. Returns the length of the textual representation.
requirements: If buf is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory of at least buf_len bytes.
buf_len must be non-negative; zero is allowed to query required length without writing (behavior inferred from typical patterns).
a must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT.
no_name nonzero typically forces dotted OID output; zero may allow names (inferred).
Caller must use the return value to detect truncation or to size buffers appropriately.

functions.name: OBJ_txt2nid
functions.description: Returns the NID corresponding to a textual object representation (name or dotted OID).
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller must check the return value; unknown inputs may map to NID_undef or -1 depending on OpenSSL, not specified here.

functions.name: OBJ_ln2nid
functions.description: Returns the NID for a long name string.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string representing a long name.
Caller must check the return value for failure (e.g., NID_undef or negative) as appropriate.

functions.name: OBJ_sn2nid
functions.description: Returns the NID for a short name string.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string representing a short name.
Caller must check the return value for failure (e.g., NID_undef or negative) as appropriate.

functions.name: OBJ_cmp
functions.description: Compares two ASN1_OBJECTs for ordering/equality. Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero depending on the comparison.
requirements: a and b must point to valid ASN1_OBJECT instances.
The return value semantics follow strcmp-style conventions; callers must not assume specific magnitude beyond sign.

functions.name: OBJ_bsearch_
functions.signature: const void *OBJ_bsearch_(const void *key, const void *base, int num, int size, int (*cmp)(const void *, const void *));
functions.description: Performs a binary search over an array using a caller-supplied comparator. Similar to standard bsearch but with OpenSSL-specific calling conventions.
requirements: base must point to an array of at least num elements, each of size bytes.
num must be non-negative; if zero, no elements are searched.
size must be the size in bytes of each array element and must be positive.
key must point to a key object comparable by cmp.
cmp must impose a total ordering compatible with the sorted order of base; it must be a valid function pointer accepting pointers to key and element and return negative/zero/positive per comparison.
The returned pointer is to a matching element or NULL if not found; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: OBJ_bsearch_ex_
functions.signature: const void *OBJ_bsearch_ex_(const void *key, const void *base, int num, int size, int (*cmp)(const void *, const void *), int flags);
functions.description: Extended binary search that supports flags to modify behavior (e.g., value-on-nomatch, first-on-match). Returns a pointer to an element or to an insertion point depending on flags.
requirements: base must point to an array of at least num elements, each of size bytes.
num must be non-negative; if zero, no elements are searched.
size must be positive and match the element size.
key must be comparable by cmp; cmp must be a valid comparator consistent with the array's sort order.
flags may include OBJ_BSEARCH_VALUE_ON_NOMATCH and OBJ_BSEARCH_FIRST_VALUE_ON_MATCH (defined in this header).
Caller must interpret the return per flags and check for NULL as needed.

functions.name: OBJ_new_nid
functions.description: Allocates/reserves a block of new NID values for application-defined objects and returns the first NID in the block.
requirements: num must be a positive integer indicating how many NIDs to reserve.
Caller must check the return value; negative or zero indicates failure (exact convention not specified here).
Reserved NIDs should be used immediately with subsequent object creation functions (e.g., OBJ_add_object/OBJ_create).

functions.name: OBJ_add_object
functions.description: Adds an ASN1_OBJECT to OpenSSL's internal object database, making it available for lookup by NID/name/OID.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT to register.
Caller must check the return value for success/non-success.
Ownership/lifetime of obj after registration is not specified here; assume the caller retains responsibility unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: OBJ_create
functions.signature: int OBJ_create(const char *oid, const char *sn, const char *ln);
functions.description: Creates and registers a new object given its dotted numeric OID and associated short and long names.
requirements: oid must be a valid dotted numeric OID string (e.g., "1.2.840.113549.1.1.5").
sn may be NULL or a valid short name string; ln may be NULL or a valid long name string (exact NULL handling not stated; inferred that names are optional in some contexts).
Caller must check the return value for success.
The newly created object becomes available for subsequent NID and name lookups.

functions.name: OBJ_create_objects
functions.description: Reads object definitions from a BIO stream and creates/registers them in the object database. The input format is OpenSSL-specific.
requirements: in must be a valid, readable BIO positioned at the start of the object definitions.
Caller must check the return value for the number of successfully created objects or for success/failure (exact semantics not fully specified here).
The input data must follow the expected format; malformed input will cause failures.

functions.name: OBJ_length
functions.description: Returns the length, in bytes, of the object identifier data contained in an ASN1_OBJECT.
requirements: obj must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT pointer.
Caller must use the return value as a size; zero may indicate an empty or invalid object (not specified).

functions.name: OBJ_get0_data
functions.description: Returns a read-only pointer to the raw object identifier data bytes of an ASN1_OBJECT.
requirements: obj must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT pointer.
Returned pointer must not be modified or freed and is only valid as long as obj remains valid.

functions.name: OBJ_find_sigid_algs
functions.description: Given a signature algorithm NID, looks up the corresponding digest and public key algorithm NIDs.
requirements: signid must be a valid signature algorithm NID.
pdig_nid and ppkey_nid may be NULL; if non-NULL, they must point to writable integers to receive results.
Caller must check the return value to determine success.

functions.name: OBJ_find_sigid_by_algs
functions.signature: int OBJ_find_sigid_by_algs(int *psignid, int dig_nid, int pkey_nid);
functions.description: Given digest and public key algorithm NIDs, looks up the composite signature algorithm NID.
requirements: psignid may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to a writable integer to receive the result.
dig_nid and pkey_nid must be valid NIDs.
Caller must check the return value to determine success.

functions.name: OBJ_add_sigid
functions.signature: int OBJ_add_sigid(int signid, int dig_id, int pkey_id);
functions.description: Registers a mapping between a signature algorithm NID and its digest and public key algorithm NIDs.
requirements: signid, dig_id, and pkey_id must be valid NIDs.
Caller must check the return value to confirm the mapping was added.

functions.name: OBJ_sigid_free
functions.description: Frees internal resources used to store signature algorithm ID mappings.
requirements: Should not be called concurrently with other operations that access or modify signature ID mappings without external synchronization.
After calling, previous lookups may be invalid until mappings are recreated.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_error
functions.description: Returns a nonzero value if the last operation on the given OPENSSL_LHASH encountered an error, otherwise 0. Intended to be checked after operations like insert/delete/retrieve.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH previously created by OPENSSL_LH_new (or a compatible typed wrapper).
Callers should check the return value (nonzero indicates an error condition on the hash table).

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_new
functions.description: Creates a new dynamic hash table using the supplied raw hash and compare callbacks. The callbacks operate on void* keys/items and are used for all key operations.
requirements: h must be a valid function pointer of type unsigned long (*)(const void *), returning a stable hash for the key.
c must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(const void *, const void *), returning 0 for equality and nonzero otherwise (OpenSSL compare convention).
The returned OPENSSL_LHASH* must be freed with OPENSSL_LH_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks
functions.signature: OPENSSL_LHASH *OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks(OPENSSL_LHASH *lh, OPENSSL_LH_HASHFUNCTHUNK hw, OPENSSL_LH_COMPFUNCTHUNK cw, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNC_THUNK daw, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG_THUNK daaw);
functions.description: Associates thunk adapters with an existing hash table to enable type-safe wrapper conversions for hash/compare and doall callbacks. Returns the same lh for chaining.
requirements: lh must be a valid OPENSSL_LHASH previously created by OPENSSL_LH_new.
hw, cw, daw, and daaw must be valid function pointers that correctly adapt from untyped (void*) callbacks to type-specific callbacks expected by the caller’s wrappers.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_free
functions.description: Frees the hash table object and its internal structures. Does not call user-defined destructors for stored items.
requirements: lh must be a pointer previously returned by OPENSSL_LH_new or compatible wrappers; after calling, lh must not be used.
Items stored in the table are not freed; the caller is responsible for freeing user data beforehand (e.g., via OPENSSL_LH_doall or custom iteration) if needed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_flush
functions.description: Removes all items from the hash table without destroying the table object, leaving it empty.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
Stored items are not freed; the caller is responsible for freeing user data if required.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_insert
functions.description: Inserts an item into the hash table. If an equal item already exists (per compare function), it is replaced and the old item is returned; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
data must be a valid pointer compatible with the table’s hash and compare callbacks (non-NULL is strongly expected).
Caller must handle the returned pointer: if non-NULL, it is the displaced previous item and must be managed/freed by the caller as appropriate.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_delete
functions.description: Deletes an item equal to 'data' from the table (as determined by the compare function) and returns the actual removed item pointer, or NULL if not found.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
data must be a valid key/item pointer comparable by the table’s compare callback.
Caller is responsible for freeing or otherwise handling the returned removed item.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_retrieve
functions.description: Looks up and returns the item equal to 'data' (per compare function), or NULL if not present.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
data must be a valid key/item pointer consistent with the table’s callbacks.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_doall
functions.description: Applies the callback 'func' to every item in the table. The callback receives each item pointer as void*.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
func must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(void *).
func must tolerate being called once per item; its behavior must not invalidate the hash table unless explicitly intended.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_doall_arg
functions.description: Applies 'func' to every item in the table, passing both the item pointer and the supplied 'arg'.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
func must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(void *, void *).
The provided 'arg' pointer must remain valid for the duration of the traversal.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_doall_arg_thunk
functions.signature: void OPENSSL_LH_doall_arg_thunk(OPENSSL_LHASH *lh, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG_THUNK daaw, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG fn, void *arg);
functions.description: Performs a typed doall-arg traversal using a thunk adapter. 'daaw' adapts the untyped node pointer and arg before invoking the user callback 'fn'.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
daaw must be a valid thunk of type void (*)(void *, void *, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG) that correctly forwards to 'fn'.
fn must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(void *, void *).
'arg' must remain valid throughout the traversal.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_strhash
functions.description: Computes and returns a hash value for a NUL-terminated C string using OpenSSL’s string hash algorithm. Useful as a hash function when storing strings in an lh table.
requirements: c must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_num_items
functions.description: Returns the number of items currently stored in the hash table.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_get_down_load
functions.description: Returns the current down_load (load factor threshold scaled by LH_LOAD_MULT) used for resizing behavior.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_set_down_load
functions.description: Sets the table’s down_load parameter (load factor threshold scaled by LH_LOAD_MULT) that controls resizing.
requirements: lh must be a valid, initialized OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.
down_load is an unsigned long; callers should use values consistent with LH_LOAD_MULT scaling (exact acceptable range is not specified here).

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_stats
functions.description: Writes overall hash table statistics to the given FILE stream. Deprecated in OpenSSL 3.1.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined and not compiled out by deprecation settings (OSSL_DEPRECATEDIN_3_1).
lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_node_stats
functions.description: Writes per-bucket node statistics to the given FILE stream. Deprecated in OpenSSL 3.1.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined and not compiled out by deprecation settings.
lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_node_usage_stats
functions.description: Writes node usage statistics (e.g., chain lengths) to the given FILE stream. Deprecated in OpenSSL 3.1.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined and not compiled out by deprecation settings.
lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_stats_bio
functions.description: Writes overall hash table statistics to the given BIO.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
out must be a valid BIO configured for output.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_node_stats_bio
functions.description: Writes per-bucket node statistics to the given BIO.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
out must be a valid BIO configured for output.

functions.name: OPENSSL_LH_node_usage_stats_bio
functions.description: Writes node usage statistics to the given BIO.
requirements: lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.
out must be a valid BIO configured for output.

functions.name: lh_error
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_error; returns whether the last table operation resulted in an error.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be a valid OPENSSL_LHASH pointer.

functions.name: lh_new
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_new; creates a new hash table with the given raw callbacks.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
h and c must be valid callback pointers as for OPENSSL_LH_new.

functions.name: lh_free
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_free; frees the hash table object (does not free stored items).
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be a pointer previously created by lh_new/OPENSSL_LH_new.

functions.name: lh_insert
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_insert; inserts or replaces an item, returning any displaced item.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; data must be compatible with the table’s callbacks.

functions.name: lh_delete
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_delete; removes and returns an item equal to 'data', or NULL if not found.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; data must be comparable by the table’s compare function.

functions.name: lh_retrieve
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_retrieve; looks up and returns the item equal to 'data'.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; data must be comparable by the table’s compare function.

functions.name: lh_doall
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_doall; applies the callback to each item in the table.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; func must be a valid void (*)(void*) pointer.

functions.name: lh_doall_arg
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_doall_arg; applies the callback with an additional argument to each item.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; func must be void (*)(void*, void*); arg must remain valid during traversal.

functions.name: lh_strhash
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_strhash; computes a hash for a NUL-terminated C string.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
c must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: lh_num_items
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_num_items; returns the number of items in the table.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be a valid pointer to an OPENSSL_LHASH.

functions.name: lh_stats
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_stats; writes overall stats to a FILE. Deprecated in 3.1.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined and OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined; also subject to deprecation settings.
lh must be valid; fp must be a valid writable FILE*.

functions.name: lh_node_stats
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_node_stats; writes per-bucket node stats to a FILE. Deprecated in 3.1.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined and OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined; also subject to deprecation settings.
lh must be valid; fp must be a valid writable FILE*.

functions.name: lh_node_usage_stats
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_node_usage_stats; writes node usage stats to a FILE. Deprecated in 3.1.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined and OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined; also subject to deprecation settings.
lh must be valid; fp must be a valid writable FILE*.

functions.name: lh_stats_bio
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_stats_bio; writes overall stats to a BIO.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined (subject to deprecation in 3.1 for some stat APIs).
lh must be valid; out must be a valid writable BIO.

functions.name: lh_node_stats_bio
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_node_stats_bio; writes per-bucket node stats to a BIO.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; out must be a valid writable BIO.

functions.name: lh_node_usage_stats_bio
functions.description: Macro alias of OPENSSL_LH_node_usage_stats_bio; writes node usage stats to a BIO.
requirements: This name is available only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_1_1_0 is not defined.
lh must be valid; out must be a valid writable BIO.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_new
functions.signature: LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING) *lh_OPENSSL_STRING_new(unsigned long (*hfn)(const OPENSSL_STRING *), int (*cmp)(const OPENSSL_STRING *, const OPENSSL_STRING *));
functions.description: Typed wrapper (macro) that creates an LHASH for OPENSSL_STRING entries with type-checked hash and compare functions. Internally uses OPENSSL_LH_new and sets thunks for type safety.
requirements: hfn must be a valid pointer to unsigned long (*)(const OPENSSL_STRING *).
cmp must be a valid pointer to int (*)(const OPENSSL_STRING *, const OPENSSL_STRING *).
Return value must be freed with lh_OPENSSL_STRING_free (or OPENSSL_LH_free via the macro).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_free
functions.description: Frees a typed OPENSSL_STRING hash table wrapper. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_free.
requirements: lh must be a LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING) created by lh_OPENSSL_STRING_new.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_flush
functions.description: Removes all items from the OPENSSL_STRING table without destroying the table object. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_flush.
requirements: lh must be a valid LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING).
Stored items are not freed automatically.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_insert
functions.description: Inserts an OPENSSL_STRING item; returns any displaced previous item (or NULL). Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_insert with type checks.
requirements: lh must be valid.
ptr must be a valid OPENSSL_STRING* compatible with the supplied hfn/cmp.
If the return value is non-NULL, caller is responsible for handling/freeing the displaced item.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_delete
functions.description: Deletes and returns an item equal to ptr (or NULL if not found). Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_delete with type checks.
requirements: lh must be valid.
ptr must be a valid key compatible with the table’s compare function.
Caller must free/manage the returned item as appropriate.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_retrieve
functions.description: Retrieves an item equal to ptr. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_retrieve with type checks.
requirements: lh must be valid.
ptr must be a valid key compatible with the table’s compare function.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_error
functions.description: Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_error for an OPENSSL_STRING table; indicates whether the last operation encountered an error.
requirements: lh must be a valid LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_num_items
functions.description: Returns the number of items in the OPENSSL_STRING table. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_num_items.
requirements: lh must be a valid LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_node_stats_bio
functions.description: Writes per-bucket node statistics for the OPENSSL_STRING table to a BIO. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_node_stats_bio.
requirements: lh must be valid.
out must be a valid writable BIO.
Subject to deprecation of stats APIs in OpenSSL 3.1.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_node_usage_stats_bio

requirements: lh must be valid.
out must be a valid writable BIO.
Subject to deprecation of stats APIs in OpenSSL 3.1.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_stats_bio
functions.description: Writes overall statistics for the OPENSSL_STRING table to a BIO. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_stats_bio.
requirements: lh must be valid.
out must be a valid writable BIO.
Subject to deprecation of stats APIs in OpenSSL 3.1.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_get_down_load
functions.description: Returns the current down_load parameter for the OPENSSL_STRING table. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_get_down_load.
requirements: lh must be a valid LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_STRING).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_set_down_load
functions.description: Sets the down_load parameter for the OPENSSL_STRING table. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_set_down_load.
requirements: lh must be valid.
dl should be a load factor scaled by LH_LOAD_MULT (exact acceptable range not specified here).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_STRING_doall
functions.description: Applies a typed callback to each OPENSSL_STRING item in the table. Macro calling OPENSSL_LH_doall via a thunk.
requirements: lh must be valid.
dfn must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(OPENSSL_STRING *).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_CSTRING_flush

requirements: lh must be a valid LHASH_OF(OPENSSL_CSTRING).

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_CSTRING_retrieve

requirements: lh must be valid.

functions.name: lh_OPENSSL_CSTRING_error

functions.name: BIO_ctrl_wpending
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes buffered for output and not yet written by the BIO.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_callback_fn
functions.signature: long BIO_callback_fn(BIO *b, int oper, const char *argp, int argi, long argl, long ret);
functions.description: Callback prototype (deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0) invoked by BIOs before and after BIO operations to observe or influence I/O. The oper argument indicates the operation (e.g., BIO_CB_READ, BIO_CB_WRITE, etc.) and includes BIO_CB_RETURN on post-call. argp/argi/argl convey operation-specific data; ret is the underlying operation’s return value on post-call. Typical usage is logging, tracing, or diagnostics via BIO_set_callback/BIO_get_callback.
requirements: Function must exactly match the signature and return type long.
The oper value may include BIO_CB_RETURN to denote post-call; callers should check with BIO_cb_pre/BIO_cb_post or BIO_CB_RETURN flag.
argp/argi/argl/ret meanings are operation-specific and may be null/unused depending on oper (details not specified in this header; unknown).
Intended to be installed via BIO_set_callback on a BIO; this typedef is deprecated in 3.0 (use BIO_callback_fn_ex).

functions.name: BIO_get_callback
functions.description: Returns the legacy BIO callback function previously set on the BIO.
requirements: Available only in builds where OpenSSL 3.0 deprecations are exposed (legacy API).
b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_set_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy BIO callback function for the BIO.
requirements: Available only in builds where OpenSSL 3.0 deprecations are exposed (legacy API).
b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_debug_callback
functions.signature: OSSL_DEPRECATEDIN_3_0 long BIO_debug_callback(BIO *bio, int cmd, const char *argp, int argi, long argl, long ret);
functions.description: A legacy debug callback helper that can be installed as a BIO callback to log operations.
requirements: Available only in builds where OpenSSL 3.0 deprecations are exposed (legacy API).
bio must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_callback_fn_ex
functions.signature: long BIO_callback_fn_ex(BIO *b, int oper, const char *argp, size_t len, int argi, long argl, int ret, size_t *processed);
functions.description: Extended BIO callback prototype used to observe BIO operations with size-aware parameters. Called before and after underlying BIO I/O; oper indicates the operation and includes BIO_CB_RETURN on post-call. argp/len/argi/argl carry operation-specific context; ret is the operation’s integer return status; processed may indicate bytes processed (library-defined). Typical usage is logging and debugging via BIO_set_callback_ex/BIO_get_callback_ex.
requirements: Function must exactly match the signature and return type long.
oper may include BIO_CB_RETURN to denote post-call; code should branch accordingly.
argp may be NULL and len may be 0 depending on oper (not specified here; unknown).
processed may be NULL or may point to a valid size_t depending on oper (not specified here; unknown).
Install via BIO_set_callback_ex on a BIO.

functions.name: BIO_get_callback_ex
functions.description: Returns the extended BIO callback function currently set for the BIO.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_set_callback_ex
functions.description: Sets the extended BIO callback for the BIO.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_debug_callback_ex
functions.signature: long BIO_debug_callback_ex(BIO *bio, int oper, const char *argp, size_t len, int argi, long argl, int ret, size_t *processed);
functions.description: A helper implementing a verbose callback suitable for BIO_set_callback_ex to log BIO operations.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO pointer.
If processed is non-NULL, it should point to writable storage for a size_t.

functions.name: BIO_get_callback_arg
functions.description: Gets the callback argument pointer associated with the BIO (legacy pattern).
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_set_callback_arg
functions.description: Sets the callback argument pointer on the BIO (legacy pattern).
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_method_name
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name of the BIO’s method.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: BIO_method_type
functions.description: Returns the BIO method type (class/type bitmask).
requirements: b must be a valid BIO pointer.

functions.name: asn1_ps_func
functions.signature: int asn1_ps_func(BIO *b, unsigned char **pbuf, int *plen, void *parg);
functions.description: Function type used by the ASN1 BIO (BIO_f_asn1) as a prefix/suffix processing callback. It can supply or modify a buffer (pbuf/plen) to be prepended/appended when encoding/decoding ASN.1 streams. Registered with BIO_asn1_set_prefix/BIO_asn1_set_suffix (and corresponding getters).
requirements: Function must match the signature and return an int status (success/failure semantics not detailed here; unknown).
When called, pbuf and plen must be treated as in/out parameters: the function may read and/or update the buffer pointer and its length (exact ownership and lifetime rules are not detailed; unknown).
parg is an opaque context pointer provided by the caller (contents unspecified).
Used only with ASN1 BIO via BIO_asn1_set_prefix/BIO_asn1_set_suffix.

functions.name: BIO_dgram_sctp_notification_handler_fn
functions.description: Callback prototype for handling SCTP notifications for datagram SCTP BIOs. Intended to be registered via BIO_dgram_sctp_notification_cb to receive SCTP control/notification messages delivered by the BIO.
requirements: Function must match the signature and return void.
context is the user-supplied pointer passed during registration; treat as opaque.
buf points to the notification buffer provided by the BIO (format/length not specified here; unknown).
Meaningful only when OpenSSL is built with SCTP support (OPENSSL_NO_SCTP not defined).
Register using BIO_dgram_sctp_notification_cb(BIO*, handler, context).

functions.name: BIO_printf
functions.description: Formatted print to a BIO, similar to printf. Returns number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
requirements: bio must be a writable BIO.
format must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with arguments.

functions.name: BIO_vprintf
functions.signature: int BIO_vprintf(BIO *bio, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: va_list variant of BIO_printf.
requirements: bio must be a writable BIO.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid va_list matching format.

functions.name: BIO_snprintf
functions.signature: int BIO_snprintf(char *buf, size_t n, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Safe snprintf-like formatter provided by OpenSSL. Writes formatted text into buf up to n bytes.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least n bytes.
format must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with arguments.

functions.name: BIO_vsnprintf
functions.signature: int BIO_vsnprintf(char *buf, size_t n, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: va_list variant of BIO_snprintf.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least n bytes.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid va_list matching format.

functions.name: BIO_set_ex_data
functions.description: Associates application-specific ex_data with a BIO at the given index.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.
idx must be a valid ex_data index obtained via BIO_get_ex_new_index/CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index.

functions.name: BIO_get_ex_data
functions.description: Retrieves application-specific ex_data associated with a BIO at the given index.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.
idx must be a valid ex_data index that was set previously.

functions.name: BIO_number_read
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes read through the BIO (cumulative counter).
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_number_written
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes written through the BIO (cumulative counter).
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_asn1_set_prefix
functions.description: Sets a prefix callback and its free callback for the ASN.1 BIO filter to prepend data before encoding.
requirements: b must be a valid ASN.1-capable BIO (BIO_f_asn1 filter).
prefix and/or prefix_free may be NULL to clear existing hooks.

functions.name: BIO_asn1_get_prefix
functions.description: Retrieves the currently set ASN.1 prefix and free callbacks for the BIO.
requirements: b must be a valid ASN.1-capable BIO.
pprefix and pprefix_free, if non-NULL, must be valid output pointers.

functions.name: BIO_asn1_set_suffix
functions.description: Sets a suffix callback and its free callback for the ASN.1 BIO filter to append data after encoding.
requirements: b must be a valid ASN.1-capable BIO.
suffix and/or suffix_free may be NULL to clear existing hooks.

functions.name: BIO_asn1_get_suffix
functions.description: Retrieves the currently set ASN.1 suffix and free callbacks for the BIO.
requirements: b must be a valid ASN.1-capable BIO.
psuffix and psuffix_free, if non-NULL, must be valid output pointers.

functions.name: BIO_s_file
functions.description: Returns the BIO_METHOD for file BIOs (BIO_s_file).

functions.name: BIO_new_file
functions.description: Creates a new file BIO by opening the specified filename with stdio mode (e.g., "r", "w").
requirements: filename must be a valid path.
mode must be a valid fopen-style mode string.

functions.name: BIO_new_from_core_bio
functions.description: Wraps a provider core BIO handle as a public BIO object.
requirements: corebio must be a valid OSSL_CORE_BIO pointer obtained from a provider.
libctx may be NULL for default library context.

functions.name: BIO_new_fp
functions.description: Creates a new BIO that wraps a FILE* stream.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_STDIO is not defined.
stream must be a valid FILE*.
close_flag controls ownership (use BIO_NOCLOSE or BIO_CLOSE semantics).

functions.name: BIO_new_ex
functions.description: Allocates a new BIO with the specified method, associated with a library context.
requirements: method must be a valid BIO_METHOD pointer.
libctx may be NULL for default context.

functions.name: BIO_new
functions.description: Allocates a new BIO using the given method.
requirements: type must be a valid BIO_METHOD pointer.

functions.name: BIO_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count and frees the BIO if it reaches zero.
requirements: a may be NULL (no-op) or a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_set_data
functions.description: Stores implementation-specific per-BIO data pointer within a BIO object.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_get_data
functions.description: Retrieves the implementation-specific per-BIO data pointer stored in the BIO.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_set_init
functions.description: Sets the init flag indicating the BIO is initialized and ready.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_get_init
functions.description: Gets the init flag from the BIO.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_set_shutdown
functions.description: Sets the shutdown flag for the BIO, controlling behavior on free/close.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_get_shutdown
functions.description: Gets the shutdown flag from the BIO.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_vfree
functions.description: Frees a BIO object (void return variant).
requirements: a may be NULL (no-op) or a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the BIO.
requirements: a must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_read
functions.description: Reads up to dlen bytes from the BIO into data. Returns number of bytes read or <=0 on error/EOF (check BIO_should_retry).
requirements: b must be a valid readable BIO.
data must point to a buffer of at least dlen bytes.
dlen must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_read_ex
functions.signature: int BIO_read_ex(BIO *b, void *data, size_t dlen, size_t *readbytes);
functions.description: Reads up to dlen bytes from the BIO into data and reports actual bytes read in readbytes. Returns 1 on success, 0/<=0 otherwise.
requirements: b must be a valid readable BIO.
data must point to a buffer of at least dlen bytes.
readbytes, if non-NULL, must be a valid pointer to size_t.

functions.name: BIO_recvmmsg
functions.signature: __owur int BIO_recvmmsg(BIO *b, BIO_MSG *msg, size_t stride, size_t num_msg, uint64_t flags, size_t *msgs_processed);
functions.description: Receives multiple datagrams/messages from a datagram-capable BIO into an array of BIO_MSG entries.
requirements: b must be a valid datagram-capable BIO.
msg must point to an array with capacity for num_msg entries with layout described by stride.
stride must be >= sizeof(BIO_MSG).
msgs_processed, if non-NULL, must be writable.

functions.name: BIO_gets
functions.description: Reads a line or up to size-1 bytes into buf, NUL-terminating. Returns number of bytes read or <=0 on error/EOF.
requirements: bp must be a valid readable BIO.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be > 0 for meaningful reads.

functions.name: BIO_get_line
functions.description: Reads a single text line from BIO into buf, up to size-1 bytes, NUL-terminating. Returns number of bytes read or <=0 on error/EOF.
requirements: bio must be a valid readable BIO.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be > 0.

functions.name: BIO_write
functions.signature: int BIO_write(BIO *b, const void *data, int dlen);
functions.description: Writes dlen bytes from data to the BIO. Returns number of bytes written or <=0 on error (check BIO_should_retry).
requirements: b must be a valid writable BIO.
data must point to at least dlen bytes.
dlen must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_write_ex
functions.signature: int BIO_write_ex(BIO *b, const void *data, size_t dlen, size_t *written);
functions.description: Writes up to dlen bytes to the BIO and sets written to the number of bytes actually written. Returns 1 on success, 0/<=0 otherwise.
requirements: b must be a valid writable BIO.
data must point to at least dlen bytes.
written, if non-NULL, must be writable.

functions.name: BIO_sendmmsg
functions.signature: __owur int BIO_sendmmsg(BIO *b, BIO_MSG *msg, size_t stride, size_t num_msg, uint64_t flags, size_t *msgs_processed);
functions.description: Sends multiple datagrams/messages via a datagram-capable BIO using an array of BIO_MSG entries.
requirements: b must be a valid datagram-capable, writable BIO.
msg must point to an array of num_msg entries.
stride must be >= sizeof(BIO_MSG).
msgs_processed, if non-NULL, must be writable.

functions.name: BIO_get_rpoll_descriptor
functions.description: Obtains a read poll descriptor for the BIO, if supported, into desc.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO.
desc must be a valid pointer to BIO_POLL_DESCRIPTOR.

functions.name: BIO_get_wpoll_descriptor
functions.description: Obtains a write poll descriptor for the BIO, if supported, into desc.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO.
desc must be a valid pointer to BIO_POLL_DESCRIPTOR.

functions.name: BIO_puts
functions.description: Writes a NUL-terminated string to the BIO.
requirements: bp must be a valid writable BIO.
buf must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: BIO_indent
functions.signature: int BIO_indent(BIO *b, int indent, int max);
functions.description: Writes indentation spaces to a BIO, up to max spaces, returning success status.
requirements: b must be a valid writable BIO.
indent and max should be non-negative; indent typically <= max.

functions.name: BIO_ctrl
functions.signature: long BIO_ctrl(BIO *bp, int cmd, long larg, void *parg);
functions.description: Generic control interface for BIOs. Performs command cmd with arguments.
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.
cmd must be a valid BIO control code for the BIO’s method.
parg usage depends on cmd; must be valid if required.

functions.name: BIO_callback_ctrl
functions.description: Control interface for setting callback functions on BIOs.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO.
cmd must be appropriate for callback control.
fp may be NULL depending on cmd.

functions.name: BIO_ptr_ctrl
functions.description: Like BIO_ctrl but returns a pointer result.
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.
cmd must be valid for pointer-returning operations.

functions.name: BIO_int_ctrl
functions.signature: long BIO_int_ctrl(BIO *bp, int cmd, long larg, int iarg);
functions.description: Like BIO_ctrl but passes an additional int argument.
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.
cmd must be valid for this use.

functions.name: BIO_push
functions.description: Pushes append onto the BIO chain before b, returning the new head.
requirements: b and append must be valid BIOs.
The resulting chain’s ownership must be managed (use BIO_free_all to free chains).

functions.name: BIO_pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the next BIO from a chain headed by b (detaches the top).
requirements: b must be a valid BIO chain head or single BIO.

functions.name: BIO_free_all
functions.description: Frees a BIO and all BIOs in its chain.
requirements: a may be NULL (no-op) or a valid BIO/chain.

functions.name: BIO_find_type
functions.description: Finds the first BIO in the chain of type bio_type (or matching classes).
requirements: b must be a valid BIO (optionally a chain).
bio_type must be a valid BIO type mask/index.

functions.name: BIO_next
functions.description: Returns the next BIO in the chain after b.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO (may be end of chain).

functions.name: BIO_set_next
functions.description: Sets the next BIO in the chain after b.
requirements: b must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_get_retry_BIO
functions.description: Walks a BIO chain to find a BIO that requires retry and sets reason to the retry code.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.
reason may be NULL or must be a valid pointer to int.

functions.name: BIO_get_retry_reason
functions.description: Returns the last retry reason set on the BIO.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_set_retry_reason
functions.description: Sets the retry reason code on the BIO.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: BIO_dup_chain
functions.description: Duplicates a BIO chain, returning a new chain with increased refs or copies depending on method.
requirements: in must be a valid BIO (optionally a chain).

functions.name: BIO_nread0
functions.description: Provides direct read access to the BIO’s internal buffer without copying; returns number of available bytes and sets buf.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO supporting nread0 semantics.
buf must be a valid pointer to char* for output.

functions.name: BIO_nread
functions.description: Reads up to num bytes from the BIO using zero-copy semantics where possible, returning number of bytes read and setting buf.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO supporting nread.
buf must be a valid pointer to char* for output.
num must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_nwrite0
functions.description: Provides direct write access to the BIO’s internal buffer; returns available space and sets buf to a writable region.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO supporting nwrite0.
buf must be a valid pointer to char* for output.

functions.name: BIO_nwrite
functions.description: Commits up to num bytes written via zero-copy semantics to the BIO.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO supporting nwrite.
buf must be a valid pointer to char* likely obtained via BIO_nwrite0.
num must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_s_connect

functions.name: BIO_s_accept
functions.description: Returns the BIO_METHOD for accept (server) socket BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_s_fd
functions.description: Returns the BIO_METHOD for file descriptor BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_s_log
functions.description: Returns the BIO_METHOD for system logging BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_s_bio
functions.description: Returns the BIO_METHOD for BIO pairs (memory-based interlinked BIOs).

functions.name: BIO_s_null

functions.name: BIO_f_buffer

functions.name: BIO_f_readbuffer
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for read-buffering filter BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_f_linebuffer
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for line-buffering filter BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_f_nbio_test
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for non-blocking I/O test filter BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_f_prefix
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for prefixing output (e.g., indentation/log prefixes).

functions.name: BIO_s_core
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD used to wrap core BIOs (provider core).

functions.name: BIO_s_dgram_pair
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for paired datagram BIOs.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_DGRAM is not defined.

functions.name: BIO_s_datagram
functions.description: Returns the BIOMETHOD for datagram (UDP) socket BIOs.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_NO_DGRAM is not defined.

functions.name: BIO_dgram_non_fatal_error

functions.name: BIO_new_dgram
