functions.name: BUF_MEM_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty BUF_MEM structure used to manage a growable memory buffer. Typical usage: call BUF_MEM_new(), then grow the buffer with BUF_MEM_grow/BUF_MEM_grow_clean as needed, and finally free it with BUF_MEM_free().
requirements: Caller must release the returned BUF_MEM* with BUF_MEM_free() to avoid memory leaks.
The returned pointer must be checked by the caller before use; allocation failure handling is required (return value may be NULL).
The BUF_MEM object must be considered uninitialized for content until grown with BUF_MEM_grow/BUF_MEM_grow_clean.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_new_ex
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new BUF_MEM structure with behavior influenced by flags (e.g., using secure memory if requested). Typical usage mirrors BUF_MEM_new(), but pass desired flags at creation. Note: Only BUF_MEM_FLAG_SECURE (0x01) is defined in this header; other flags, if any, are unknown here.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid combination of flags; recognized in this header: BUF_MEM_FLAG_SECURE (0x01). Semantics of other values are unknown.
Caller must release the returned BUF_MEM* with BUF_MEM_free() to avoid memory leaks.
The returned pointer must be checked by the caller before use; allocation failure handling is required (return value may be NULL).
The BUF_MEM object’s buffer content is unspecified until grown with BUF_MEM_grow/BUF_MEM_grow_clean.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_free
functions.description: Frees a BUF_MEM structure previously allocated by BUF_MEM_new() or BUF_MEM_new_ex(). After this call, the pointer must not be used. Behavior for a == NULL is not specified in this header.
requirements: Parameter a must point to a valid BUF_MEM previously allocated by BUF_MEM_new() or BUF_MEM_new_ex().
Do not use the BUF_MEM object after calling BUF_MEM_free() (no use-after-free).
Do not call BUF_MEM_free() more than once on the same BUF_MEM pointer (no double-free).
The behavior when a == NULL is unspecified in this header; callers should avoid passing NULL unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_grow
functions.description: Resizes the internal buffer managed by str to exactly len bytes, growing or shrinking as needed. Newly added bytes (if the buffer grows) are not guaranteed to be zeroed; use BUF_MEM_grow_clean() if zero-initialization of new space is required. The underlying data pointer may change.
requirements: Parameter str must be a valid BUF_MEM* returned by BUF_MEM_new()/BUF_MEM_new_ex() and not yet freed.
Callers must not rely on any previous str->data pointer remaining valid across this call; it may be reallocated.
Parameter len specifies the target size in bytes; callers must ensure len is correct for their use and handle potential allocation failure (return value should be checked).
Existing data beyond the new size may be discarded when shrinking; callers must not access data beyond len after resizing.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_grow_clean
functions.description: Resizes the internal buffer to len bytes, similar to BUF_MEM_grow(), but ensures any newly allocated portion is zero-initialized. Useful when growing buffers that will hold sensitive data. The underlying data pointer may change.
requirements: Parameter str must be a valid BUF_MEM* returned by BUF_MEM_new()/BUF_MEM_new_ex() and not yet freed.
Callers must not rely on any previous str->data pointer remaining valid across this call; it may be reallocated.
Parameter len specifies the target size in bytes; callers must ensure len is correct for their use and handle potential allocation failure (return value should be checked).
When shrinking, data beyond len must not be accessed after resizing.

functions.name: BUF_reverse
functions.signature: void BUF_reverse(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, size_t siz);
functions.description: Reverses the order of bytes from the input buffer in to the output buffer out over siz bytes (i.e., out[i] = in[siz-1-i]). Often used for endianness conversions or reversing big/little-endian representations.
requirements: Parameter out must point to a writable buffer of at least siz bytes.
Parameter in must point to a readable buffer of at least siz bytes.
Pointers out and in must be valid for the specified range; overlapping behavior (e.g., in == out) is not specified in this header and should be avoided unless documented elsewhere.
If siz is nonzero, out and in must be non-NULL.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_set_default_search_path
functions.description: Sets the default search path used to locate providers for the given OpenSSL library context. Use this early to direct OpenSSL where to find provider modules before loading them.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX pointer (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
path should be a valid filesystem path string; encoding/format specifics are not documented here.
Should be called before providers are loaded and before the context is in use by multiple threads (inferred from related configuration guidance).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get0_default_search_path
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current default provider search path for the specified library context. The returned pointer is owned by the library (get0 semantics) and must not be freed or modified by the caller.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX pointer (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
The returned string is a borrowed, read-only pointer that must not be freed or modified (inferred from get0 naming pattern).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_load
functions.description: Loads (and returns a handle to) a provider with the given name into the specified library context. Typical usage is to make cryptographic algorithms from that provider available.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
name must identify an available provider (e.g., "default", "legacy", etc.); exact accepted names depend on the OpenSSL build and configuration.
The returned OSSL_PROVIDER* must later be released with OSSL_PROVIDER_unload when no longer needed.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_load_ex
functions.description: Loads a provider like OSSL_PROVIDER_load, supplying optional load parameters via an OSSL_PARAM array.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
name must identify an available provider.
params may be NULL or must point to a properly terminated OSSL_PARAM array accepted by the provider; exact expected keys and types are provider-specific and not documented here.
The returned OSSL_PROVIDER* must be released with OSSL_PROVIDER_unload.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_try_load
functions.description: Attempts to load a provider by name into the given context without failing hard if unavailable. The retain_fallbacks flag adjusts fallback behavior (semantics not fully documented here).
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
name must be a provider name string.
retain_fallbacks usage/semantics are not specified in this header; behavior is provider/framework-defined and thus unknown.
If successful, the returned handle must be released with OSSL_PROVIDER_unload.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_try_load_ex
functions.signature: OSSL_PROVIDER *OSSL_PROVIDER_try_load_ex(OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *name, OSSL_PARAM *params, int retain_fallbacks);
functions.description: Attempts to load a provider with optional parameters, adjusting fallback behavior via retain_fallbacks. Intended as a non-fatal load attempt; detailed semantics of retain_fallbacks are not specified here.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
name must identify the provider to attempt to load.
params may be NULL or must be a valid OSSL_PARAM array the provider understands.
retain_fallbacks semantics are unspecified in this header; treat as provider/framework-defined.
On success, the returned handle must be released with OSSL_PROVIDER_unload.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_unload
functions.description: Unloads a previously loaded provider and releases associated resources in the given context.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle previously obtained from a successful load function.
After successful unload, prov must not be used again.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_available
functions.description: Checks whether a provider with the given name is available in the specified library context.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX (unknown whether NULL selects the default context).
name must be a provider name string.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_do_all
functions.description: Iterates over providers in the given context and invokes the supplied callback for each one, passing cbdata through.
requirements: ctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX.
cb must be a valid function pointer compatible with the declared signature.
cbdata is passed as-is to each callback invocation.
Callback return value handling (e.g., to continue/stop) is not documented here; callers should not rely on specific control semantics without consulting full documentation.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_gettable_params
functions.description: Returns a description array of parameters that can be queried from the specified provider via OSSL_PROVIDER_get_params. The returned array is library-owned (get0-like) and read-only.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
The returned OSSL_PARAM descriptor array must not be modified or freed by the caller (inferred from gettable semantics).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get_params
functions.description: Retrieves provider parameters into the provided OSSL_PARAM array according to what the provider supports (as advertised by OSSL_PROVIDER_gettable_params).
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
params must point to a properly prepared, terminator-terminated OSSL_PARAM array whose keys/types match the provider’s gettable params.
For parameters that return pointers, ownership/validity rules follow provider definitions and are not documented here.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_self_test
functions.description: Triggers the provider’s self tests, returning success/failure. Useful for verifying a provider’s integrity or algorithm tests at runtime.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
Behavior and side effects depend on the provider; specific tests and reporting are not described here.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities
functions.signature: int OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities(const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov, const char *capability, OSSL_CALLBACK *cb, void *arg);
functions.description: Queries the provider for items of a named capability and delivers them to the supplied callback. Used to enumerate provider-specific features or data for the given capability name.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
capability must be a non-NULL capability name string understood by the provider.
cb must be a valid callback function pointer; it will be invoked to process returned capability data.
arg is an opaque pointer passed to each callback invocation.
Exact callback calling convention and parameter content are provider-defined and not described here.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_add_conf_parameter
functions.description: Associates a configuration parameter (name=value) with the given provider programmatically (in addition to configuration files). Only UTF8-string values are supported. Intended to be set early, before multi-threaded use.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
name must be a parameter name string.
value must be a UTF8 string value (only UTF8-string values are supported).
Should be called early in the main program before the provider is in use by multiple threads (per comment).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get_conf_parameters
functions.description: Retrieves requested configuration parameters (previously set via config file or OSSL_PROVIDER_add_conf_parameter) for the given provider into the provided OSSL_PARAM array. Returned values are by reference.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
params must be an array of OSSL_PARAM elements with type OSSL_PARAM_UTF8_PTR for each requested item (MUST have type OSSL_PARAM_UTF8_PTR).
Values are returned by reference, not copies; the caller must not free or modify the referenced storage unless explicitly documented elsewhere.
The params array must be properly terminated.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_conf_get_bool
functions.signature: int OSSL_PROVIDER_conf_get_bool(const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov, const char *name, int defval);
functions.description: Parses a provider configuration parameter as a boolean and returns its value; if the parameter cannot be retrieved or parsed, returns defval. Recognizes true forms like "1", "yes", "true" and false forms like "0", "no", "false".
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
name must be the configuration parameter name string.
defval supplies the default boolean value to return if retrieval/parsing fails.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_query_operation
functions.signature: const OSSL_ALGORITHM *OSSL_PROVIDER_query_operation(const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov, int operation_id, int *no_cache);
functions.description: Queries the provider for algorithms implementing the specified operation ID. Returns a provider-owned array of OSSL_ALGORITHM descriptors. no_cache can be set by the provider to advise the caller about caching behavior.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
operation_id must be an operation identifier understood by the provider.
no_cache may be NULL or must point to an int where advice will be stored.
The returned OSSL_ALGORITHM array is provider-owned; it must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Callers should pair with OSSL_PROVIDER_unquery_operation when done with the returned algorithms (inferred from the API pair).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_unquery_operation
functions.signature: void OSSL_PROVIDER_unquery_operation(const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov, int operation_id, const OSSL_ALGORITHM *algs);
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a prior OSSL_PROVIDER_query_operation for the given provider and operation, using the OSSL_ALGORITHM array previously returned.
requirements: prov must be the same provider handle used with OSSL_PROVIDER_query_operation.
operation_id should match the ID used in the corresponding query (inferred pairing).
algs must be the exact pointer previously returned by OSSL_PROVIDER_query_operation for this provider and operation.
After calling, the algs pointer must no longer be used.

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get0_provider_ctx
functions.description: Returns the provider’s opaque context pointer. The pointer is owned by the provider (get0 semantics) and is for read-only/opaque use by integrators; it must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
The returned pointer is borrowed and must not be freed or modified (inferred from get0 naming and opaque context).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get0_dispatch
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the provider’s core dispatch table. The table is provider-owned (get0 semantics) and read-only.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
The returned dispatch table pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller (inferred from get0 naming pattern).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_add_builtin
functions.description: Registers a built-in provider with the given name and initialization function in the specified library context. This allows embedding providers without dynamic loading.
requirements: libctx must be a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX.
name must be the provider name string to register.
init_fn must be a valid provider initialization function matching OSSL_provider_init_fn signature.
Should be called during initialization before attempts to load the provider dynamically (timing not strictly documented but implied by purpose).

functions.name: OSSL_PROVIDER_get0_name
functions.description: Returns the provider’s name string. The returned pointer is owned by the provider/library (get0 semantics) and must not be freed or modified.
requirements: prov must be a valid provider handle.
The returned name string is a borrowed, read-only pointer that must not be freed or modified (inferred from get0 naming pattern).

functions.name: OCSP_sendreq_new
functions.signature: OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX *OCSP_sendreq_new(BIO *io, const char *path, const OCSP_REQUEST *req, int buf_size);
functions.description: Creates and initializes an HTTP request context for sending an OCSP request over the given BIO transport. Typically used to prepare a non-blocking OCSP POST to the responder at the provided path, carrying the DER of req.
requirements: io must be a valid, connected BIO suitable for HTTP I/O.
path should be a non-NULL OCSP responder path (e.g., "/ocsp").
req should point to a valid OCSP_REQUEST to be sent; it is not modified.
buf_size should be non-negative; unknown behavior for negative values.
The returned context must be freed with OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_free (or OCSP_REQ_CTX_free alias in deprecated API).

functions.name: OCSP_sendreq_bio
functions.description: Sends an OCSP request over the given BIO to the responder path and returns the parsed OCSP_RESPONSE on success. Provides a blocking convenience wrapper for one-shot OCSP HTTP exchange.
requirements: b must be a valid, connected BIO for HTTP to the OCSP responder.
path should be a non-NULL responder path (e.g., "/ocsp").
req must point to a valid OCSP_REQUEST; ownership remains with the caller.
On failure, returns NULL; caller must handle errors via ERR_get_error().
On success, caller owns the returned OCSP_RESPONSE and must free it with OCSP_RESPONSE_free.

functions.name: OCSP_cert_to_id
functions.signature: OCSP_CERTID *OCSP_cert_to_id(const EVP_MD *dgst, const X509 *subject, const X509 *issuer);
functions.description: Constructs an OCSP_CERTID for a subject certificate using its issuer certificate and an optional digest algorithm. Used to identify a certificate in an OCSP request.
requirements: subject must be a valid X509 certificate for which status will be requested.
issuer must be the issuer certificate of subject.
dgst may be NULL to use a library default; specific default is not stated here.
Returns a newly allocated OCSP_CERTID on success; caller must free with OCSP_CERTID_free.

functions.name: OCSP_cert_id_new
functions.signature: OCSP_CERTID *OCSP_cert_id_new(const EVP_MD *dgst, const X509_NAME *issuerName, const ASN1_BIT_STRING *issuerKey, const ASN1_INTEGER *serialNumber);
functions.description: Creates an OCSP_CERTID from explicit issuer name, issuer key hash input, and certificate serial number, optionally using the specified digest algorithm. Used when caller has the issuer fields and serial number rather than full X509 objects.
requirements: issuerName, issuerKey, and serialNumber must be valid pointers to the respective ASN.1 structures describing the certificate’s issuer and serial.
dgst may be NULL to use a library default; exact default is unspecified here.
Returns a newly allocated OCSP_CERTID; caller must free with OCSP_CERTID_free.

functions.name: OCSP_request_add0_id
functions.description: Appends a certificate ID (cid) to an OCSP request as a new single request. The add0 convention indicates the request will directly reference the provided cid pointer without copying.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
cid must be a valid OCSP_CERTID; on success, ownership is transferred to req and the caller must not free cid separately.
Returns the created OCSP_ONEREQ on success, or NULL on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_request_add1_nonce
functions.signature: int OCSP_request_add1_nonce(OCSP_REQUEST *req, unsigned char *val, int len);
functions.description: Adds a nonce extension to an OCSP request, copying the provided value. If val/len usage supports defaults, that behavior is not specified here.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
If val is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes; those bytes are copied into the request.
Return value: 1 for success, 0 for failure.
Exact rules for val==NULL or len values are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_basic_add1_nonce
functions.signature: int OCSP_basic_add1_nonce(OCSP_BASICRESP *resp, unsigned char *val, int len);
functions.description: Adds a nonce extension to an OCSP basic response, copying the provided value. Commonly used to echo the request nonce or set a new one.
requirements: resp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
If val is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes; those bytes are copied into the response.
Return value: 1 for success, 0 for failure.
Exact behavior for val==NULL or special len values is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_check_nonce
functions.description: Compares the nonce in the request with the nonce in the basic response to detect replay or mismatched responses.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Return semantics (e.g., 1 match, 0 no match, negative for error) are not defined in this header (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_copy_nonce
functions.description: Copies the nonce from an OCSP request into a basic response. Useful when constructing a response that must echo a client's nonce.
requirements: resp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP to receive the nonce.
req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST containing the nonce to copy.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (exact semantics beyond boolean success not specified).

functions.name: OCSP_request_set1_name
functions.description: Sets the requestorName in an OCSP request to the provided X509_NAME, copying it (add1 semantics).
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
nm must be a valid X509_NAME. The function copies or increments reference (exact mechanism internal), so caller retains its own object.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_request_add1_cert
functions.description: Adds a copy/reference of a certificate to an OCSP request (typically to include the signer or additional certs). Uses add1 semantics (does not take ownership of caller’s pointer).
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate. The request takes a copy or ref; caller retains its own ownership of cert.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_request_sign
functions.signature: int OCSP_request_sign(OCSP_REQUEST *req, X509 *signer, EVP_PKEY *key, const EVP_MD *dgst, STACK_OF(X509) *certs, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Signs an OCSP request using the provided signer certificate and private key, optionally specifying a digest and attaching extra certificates. Flags control signature/encoding options.
requirements: req must be initialized and contain the desired request data/ids.
signer must be a valid X509 certificate corresponding to key.
key must be a valid private key matching signer’s public key.
dgst may be NULL to use default; exact default unspecified.
certs may be NULL or a valid stack of X509 to include; ownership is not transferred.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_response_status
functions.description: Returns the OCSP responder status code from an OCSP_RESPONSE (e.g., OCSP_RESPONSE_STATUS_SUCCESSFUL, ...).
requirements: resp must be a valid OCSP_RESPONSE.
On error or NULL input behavior is unspecified here; caller should check return value against defined status constants.

functions.name: OCSP_response_get1_basic
functions.description: Extracts and returns the basic OCSP response (tbsResponseData and signature) from an OCSP_RESPONSE, increasing the reference or copying so the caller owns the result.
requirements: resp must be a valid OCSP_RESPONSE that contains a basic response.
Returns a newly allocated/owned OCSP_BASICRESP on success; caller must free with OCSP_BASICRESP_free.
Returns NULL on failure or if no basic response is present.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_signature
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the signature (OCTET STRING) of the basic OCSP response. get0 indicates a non-owning pointer into bs.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Returned pointer is valid as long as bs remains valid; do not free it.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_tbs_sigalg
functions.description: Returns the signature algorithm for the to-be-signed portion of the basic response. get0 indicates a non-owning pointer.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Returned pointer is owned by bs; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_respdata
functions.description: Returns a non-owning pointer to the response data (ResponderID, producedAt, SingleResponses, etc.) inside the basic response.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Returned pointer is valid while bs is valid; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_signer
functions.description: Finds the certificate that signed the basic response, optionally searching extra_certs. On success, sets *signer to point to the signer certificate (non-owning or owning behavior unspecified here).
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
signer must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result on success.
extra_certs may be NULL or a valid stack of X509 to search.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Ownership/reference semantics of *signer are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_resp_count
functions.description: Returns the number of SingleResponse entries contained in the basic response.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Returns a non-negative count on success; negative values (if any) indicate error (unspecified).

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0
functions.description: Returns the SingleResponse at the given index from the basic response. get0 indicates a non-owning pointer.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
idx must be in the range [0, OCSP_resp_count(bs)-1]; out-of-range returns NULL.
Returned OCSP_SINGLERESP is owned by bs; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_produced_at
functions.description: Returns the producedAt timestamp of the basic response as a non-owning ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME pointer.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Return is owned by bs; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_certs
functions.description: Returns the stack of certificates embedded in the basic response, if any, as a non-owning pointer.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
Returned stack is owned by bs; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get0_id
functions.signature: int OCSP_resp_get0_id(const OCSP_BASICRESP *bs, const ASN1_OCTET_STRING **pid, const X509_NAME **pname);
functions.description: Returns the ResponderID of the basic response, either byName or byKey. On success, fills either pname or pid with non-owning pointers.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
pid and/or pname may be non-NULL to receive pointers; outputs are owned by bs and must not be freed.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_get1_id
functions.description: Returns a copy/owned reference of the ResponderID from the basic response, storing into pid and/or pname with add1 semantics so the caller owns the results.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
pid and/or pname may be non-NULL; on success, caller owns returned objects and must free them with ASN1_OCTET_STRING_free and X509_NAME_free respectively.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_resp_find
functions.description: Searches for a SingleResponse matching the given certificate ID in the basic response, starting after index 'last'. Returns the index of the next match or a negative value if not found.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
id must be a valid OCSP_CERTID to match.
last should be -1 to start from the beginning, or a previous index to continue search; behavior otherwise unsurprising.
Return value semantics beyond match index vs not found are not specified in the header (exact negative code unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_single_get0_status
functions.signature: int OCSP_single_get0_status(OCSP_SINGLERESP *single, int *reason, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **revtime, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **thisupd, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **nextupd);
functions.description: Retrieves the certificate status and associated timing and reason fields from a SingleResponse. get0 indicates returned time pointers are non-owning.
requirements: single must be a valid OCSP_SINGLERESP.
reason, revtime, thisupd, nextupd may be NULL or pointers to receive results; returned ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME pointers are owned by single and must not be freed.
Return value details (e.g., maps to V_OCSP_CERTSTATUS_* constants) are not defined here (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_resp_find_status
functions.signature: int OCSP_resp_find_status(OCSP_BASICRESP *bs, OCSP_CERTID *id, int *status, int *reason, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **revtime, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **thisupd, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME **nextupd);
functions.description: Convenience to locate a SingleResponse for a given certificate ID and extract its status, reason, and timing fields from a basic response.
requirements: bs must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
id must be a valid OCSP_CERTID to match.
status, reason, revtime, thisupd, nextupd may be NULL or valid pointers to receive results; time pointers are non-owning.
Return value semantics beyond boolean/int success are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_check_validity
functions.signature: int OCSP_check_validity(ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME *thisupd, ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME *nextupd, long sec, long maxsec);
functions.description: Checks whether the provided thisUpdate/nextUpdate timestamps indicate the response is currently valid, allowing for tolerances specified by sec and maxsec.
requirements: thisupd must be a valid ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME; nextupd may be NULL depending on usage.
sec and maxsec define allowed clock skew or freshness; exact interpretation not specified here.
Returns 1 for valid, 0 for invalid, with error specifics unspecified.

functions.name: OCSP_request_verify
functions.signature: int OCSP_request_verify(OCSP_REQUEST *req, STACK_OF(X509) *certs, X509_STORE *store, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Verifies the signature and validity of an OCSP request using the supplied cert chain and trust store, applying verification flags.
requirements: req must be a valid, possibly signed OCSP_REQUEST.
certs may be NULL or a valid STACK_OF(X509) with candidate signer certs.
store must be a valid X509_STORE with trust anchors and policies for verification.
flags controls verification behavior; specific flags not detailed here.
Returns 1 on successful verification, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_id_issuer_cmp
functions.description: Compares two OCSP certificate IDs for equality of issuer fields (name/key hash), ignoring serial numbers.
requirements: a and b must be valid OCSP_CERTID pointers.
Return value semantics (0 equal vs non-zero) not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_id_cmp
functions.description: Compares two OCSP certificate IDs for full equality including serial numbers.
requirements: a and b must be valid OCSP_CERTID pointers.
Return value semantics (0 equal vs non-zero) not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: OCSP_request_onereq_count
functions.description: Returns the number of OCSP single requests contained in the OCSP request.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
Returns non-negative count on success; negative/error semantics not specified.

functions.name: OCSP_request_onereq_get0
functions.description: Returns the i-th OCSP_ONEREQ (single request) within the given OCSP request as a non-owning pointer.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
i must be in [0, OCSP_request_onereq_count(req)-1]; out of range returns NULL.
Returned OCSP_ONEREQ is owned by req; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_onereq_get0_id
functions.description: Returns the OCSP_CERTID contained in a single request as a non-owning pointer.
requirements: one must be a valid OCSP_ONEREQ.
Returned OCSP_CERTID is owned by the OCSP_ONEREQ; do not free.

functions.name: OCSP_id_get0_info
functions.signature: int OCSP_id_get0_info(ASN1_OCTET_STRING **piNameHash, ASN1_OBJECT **pmd, ASN1_OCTET_STRING **pikeyHash, ASN1_INTEGER **pserial, OCSP_CERTID *cid);
functions.description: Extracts the internal fields of an OCSP_CERTID (issuer name hash, hash algorithm OID, issuer key hash, and serial number) as non-owning pointers.
requirements: cid must be a valid OCSP_CERTID.
Any of piNameHash, pmd, pikeyHash, pserial may be NULL or pointers to receive fields; returned pointers are owned by cid and must not be freed.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_request_is_signed
functions.description: Checks whether the OCSP request contains a signature.
requirements: req must be a valid OCSP_REQUEST.
Returns 1 if signed, 0 if not signed; error semantics not specified.

functions.name: OCSP_response_create
functions.description: Creates an OCSP_RESPONSE with the given top-level status and an optional attached basic response.
requirements: status must be one of OCSP_RESPONSE_STATUS_* constants.
bs may be NULL or a valid OCSP_BASICRESP to include.
Returns a newly allocated OCSP_RESPONSE on success; caller must free with OCSP_RESPONSE_free.

functions.name: OCSP_basic_add1_status
functions.signature: OCSP_SINGLERESP *OCSP_basic_add1_status(OCSP_BASICRESP *rsp, OCSP_CERTID *cid, int status, int reason, ASN1_TIME *revtime, ASN1_TIME *thisupd, ASN1_TIME *nextupd);
functions.description: Adds a new SingleResponse to a basic response for the given certificate ID with the specified status and timing fields. add1 indicates cid is copied or referenced so caller retains ownership.
requirements: rsp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP under construction.
cid must be a valid OCSP_CERTID; ownership is not transferred (add1 semantics).
status must be one of V_OCSP_CERTSTATUS_* constants.
reason should be a CRL reason code or -1 if not applicable; exact accepted values beyond constants are not specified here.
revtime, thisupd, nextupd may be NULL or valid ASN1_TIME pointers as appropriate.
Returns the new OCSP_SINGLERESP on success, or NULL on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_basic_add1_cert
functions.description: Adds a certificate to the basic OCSP response’s certificate list using add1 semantics (caller retains ownership of cert).
requirements: resp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_basic_sign
functions.signature: int OCSP_basic_sign(OCSP_BASICRESP *brsp, X509 *signer, EVP_PKEY *key, const EVP_MD *dgst, STACK_OF(X509) *certs, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Signs a basic OCSP response with the provided signer certificate and private key, optionally attaching extra certificates and specifying a digest and flags.
requirements: brsp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP populated with SingleResponses.
signer must be a valid X509 cert matching key.
key must be a valid private key.
dgst may be NULL to use default; exact default unspecified.
certs may be NULL or a stack of X509 to include; ownership not transferred.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_basic_sign_ctx
functions.signature: int OCSP_basic_sign_ctx(OCSP_BASICRESP *brsp, X509 *signer, EVP_MD_CTX *ctx, STACK_OF(X509) *certs, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Signs a basic OCSP response using a pre-initialized EVP_MD_CTX (for advanced signing control), with optional extra certs and flags.
requirements: brsp must be a valid OCSP_BASICRESP.
signer must be a valid X509 cert corresponding to the key configured in ctx.
ctx must be a properly initialized EVP_MD_CTX for signing before the call.
certs may be NULL or a stack of X509 to include.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_RESPID_set_by_name
functions.description: Sets the OCSP responder ID to byName using the subject name from the given certificate.
requirements: respid must be a valid OCSP_RESPID object.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_RESPID_set_by_key_ex
functions.signature: int OCSP_RESPID_set_by_key_ex(OCSP_RESPID *respid, X509 *cert, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq);
functions.description: Sets the OCSP responder ID to byKey using the subject public key from cert, with library context and property query to select algorithms/providers.
requirements: respid must be a valid OCSP_RESPID.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.
libctx may be NULL or a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX; propq may be NULL or a property query string.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_RESPID_set_by_key
functions.description: Sets the OCSP responder ID to byKey using the subject public key from cert (default library context).
requirements: respid must be a valid OCSP_RESPID.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: OCSP_RESPID_match_ex
functions.signature: int OCSP_RESPID_match_ex(OCSP_RESPID *respid, X509 *cert, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq);
functions.description: Matches the provided OCSP_RESPID against cert (byName or byKey), using the given library context and property query to select algorithms/providers.
requirements: respid must be a valid OCSP_RESPID.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.
libctx may be NULL or a valid OSSL_LIB_CTX; propq may be NULL or a property query string.
Returns 1 if match, 0 if not; error semantics beyond boolean not specified.

functions.name: OCSP_RESPID_match
functions.description: Matches the provided OCSP_RESPID against cert (byName or byKey) using default context.
requirements: respid must be a valid OCSP_RESPID.
cert must be a valid X509 certificate.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_open
functions.signature: OSSL_STORE_CTX *OSSL_STORE_open(const char *uri, const UI_METHOD *ui_method, void *ui_data, OSSL_STORE_post_process_info_fn post_process, void *post_process_data);
functions.description: Opens a STORE loader channel for the given URI and returns a context used to read objects (keys, certs, CRLs, etc.). If the loader requires user input (e.g., password/PIN), the provided UI method and data are used. Optionally, a post-process callback can modify or discard each OSSL_STORE_INFO as it’s read.
requirements: uri must reference a resource supported by an available STORE loader (scheme is inferred from the URI).
If ui_method is non-NULL, it must remain valid for the lifetime of the context; ui_data is passed back to that method as provided.
If post_process is non-NULL, it may return NULL to drop an item; its post_process_data is passed to each invocation.
On success, the returned OSSL_STORE_CTX must be closed with OSSL_STORE_close().
Errors are indicated by a NULL return; callers should not use the context if NULL is returned.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_open_ex
functions.signature: OSSL_STORE_CTX *OSSL_STORE_open_ex(const char *uri, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq, const UI_METHOD *ui_method, void *ui_data, const OSSL_PARAM params[], OSSL_STORE_post_process_info_fn post_process, void *post_process_data);
functions.description: Extended open that additionally binds to a specific library context, property query string, and optional loader parameters. Otherwise behaves like OSSL_STORE_open with UI handling and optional post-processing.
requirements: uri must specify a supported scheme.
libctx and propq may be NULL to use defaults.
params may be NULL or a parameter array understood by the selected loader; unrecognized parameters are ignored or cause open to fail depending on the loader (exact behavior is loader-specific).
If ui_method is provided, it and ui_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the context.
post_process/post_process_data semantics are the same as OSSL_STORE_open.
Returned context must be closed with OSSL_STORE_close(); NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_ctrl
functions.description: Deprecated control interface to adjust loader-specific options for an open STORE context. The meaning of cmd and any variadic arguments is loader-dependent; some common commands may be supported.
requirements: Available only when not compiled with OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0; otherwise absent.
ctx must be a valid OSSL_STORE_CTX returned by OSSL_STORE_open/Open_ex/attach.
cmd selects the control operation; required argument types and counts depend on cmd and the underlying loader. The caller must pass arguments matching the expected types for that cmd.
Returns an int status as defined by the loader; callers must check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_vctrl
functions.signature: int OSSL_STORE_vctrl(OSSL_STORE_CTX *ctx, int cmd, va_list args);
functions.description: Deprecated va_list form of OSSL_STORE_ctrl for forwarding pre-built argument lists to a loader-specific control command.
requirements: Available only when not compiled with OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0.
ctx must be a valid OSSL_STORE_CTX.
cmd selects the control operation; args must be a va_list containing the arguments expected by that cmd and loader.
Return value semantics are loader-defined; callers must check for success/failure.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_load
functions.description: Reads the next available item from the open STORE channel, returning it as an OSSL_STORE_INFO wrapper. The item can be a key, certificate, CRL, parameters, etc. A post-process callback (if provided at open time) is applied before the item is returned.
requirements: ctx must be a valid open OSSL_STORE_CTX.

Returns NULL on error, ambiguity, or if no item is produced by post-processing (e.g., callback returns NULL). Callers should use OSSL_STORE_error() and OSSL_STORE_eof() to distinguish error/end-of-data.
Each non-NULL returned OSSL_STORE_INFO must be freed with OSSL_STORE_INFO_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_delete
functions.signature: int OSSL_STORE_delete(const char *uri, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq, const UI_METHOD *ui_method, void *ui_data, const OSSL_PARAM params[]);
functions.description: Deletes an object identified by the given URI via a suitable STORE loader. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. Supports optional library context, property query, UI handling, and loader parameters.
requirements: uri must specify a deletable object using a scheme supported by a loader that implements deletion.
libctx and propq may be NULL.
params may be NULL or a loader-specific parameter array.
If the loader requires user input, ui_method/ui_data are used and must remain valid during the call.
Callers must check the int return (1 success, 0 failure).

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_eof
functions.description: Checks whether the end of data has been reached on the STORE channel.
requirements: ctx must be a valid OSSL_STORE_CTX.
Returns 1 if end-of-data, 0 otherwise; callers should not assume that 0 implies no error—use OSSL_STORE_error() to check for errors.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_error
functions.description: Indicates whether an error has occurred on the STORE channel.
requirements: ctx must be a valid OSSL_STORE_CTX.
Returns 1 if an error occurred, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_close
functions.description: Closes a STORE channel and frees associated resources.
requirements: ctx must be a context returned by a successful open/attach (may be NULL only if caller intentionally passes NULL—behavior then is unspecified by this header).
Must be called once to release the context; after closing, ctx must not be used.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_attach
functions.signature: OSSL_STORE_CTX *OSSL_STORE_attach(BIO *bio, const char *scheme, OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx, const char *propq, const UI_METHOD *ui_method, void *ui_data, const OSSL_PARAM params[], OSSL_STORE_post_process_info_fn post_process, void *post_process_data);
functions.description: Attaches a STORE loader to an existing BIO instead of a URI, using the specified scheme for interpretation. Supports optional libctx/propq, UI, parameters, and post-processing. Considered unsafe depending on the BIO’s source.
requirements: bio must be a valid, readable BIO producing data compatible with the specified scheme.
scheme must name a supported STORE loader scheme; it is used to select the loader since no URI is provided.
libctx/propq and params are optional and loader-specific.
If provided, ui_method/ui_data must remain valid for the context lifetime.
Returned context must be closed with OSSL_STORE_close(); NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_SEARCH_by_name

functions.name: OSSL_STORE_find

requirements: ctx must be a valid OSSL_STORE_CTX.

functions.name: TS_MSG_IMPRINT_get_msg

requirements: a must be a valid TS_MSG_IMPRINT pointer.

functions.name: TS_REQ_set_policy_id

requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
policy must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT OID; ownership semantics not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_policy_id
functions.description: Gets the TSA policy OID from the request.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_REQ_set_nonce
functions.description: Sets the nonce value for the TS request.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
nonce must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_nonce
functions.description: Gets the nonce value from the TS request.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_REQ_set_cert_req
functions.description: Sets the cert_req flag indicating whether the TSA should include its certificate in the response.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_cert_req
functions.description: Gets the cert_req flag from a TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_exts
functions.description: Returns the extension stack for a TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
Returned stack is owned by a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_REQ_ext_free
functions.description: Frees the extensions contained in a TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
Only frees extensions within a; a itself remains valid.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext_count
functions.description: Returns the number of extensions in the TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext_by_NID
functions.signature: int TS_REQ_get_ext_by_NID(TS_REQ *a, int nid, int lastpos);
functions.description: Finds an extension index by NID in the TS_REQ, starting after lastpos.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
nid must be a valid extension NID.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext_by_OBJ
functions.signature: int TS_REQ_get_ext_by_OBJ(TS_REQ *a, const ASN1_OBJECT *obj, int lastpos);
functions.description: Finds an extension index by object OID in the TS_REQ, starting after lastpos.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
obj must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT pointer.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext_by_critical
functions.signature: int TS_REQ_get_ext_by_critical(TS_REQ *a, int crit, int lastpos);
functions.description: Finds the next extension index in the TS_REQ matching the critical flag, starting after lastpos.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
crit should be 0 or 1.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext
functions.description: Retrieves an extension at index loc from the TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
loc must be a valid index into the extensions array.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_REQ_delete_ext
functions.description: Removes and returns the extension at index loc from the TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
loc must be a valid index.
Caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned X509_EXTENSION.

functions.name: TS_REQ_add_ext
functions.description: Adds an X509 extension to the TS_REQ at the specified position.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
ex must be a valid, dynamically allocated X509_EXTENSION; ownership is transferred to a on success.
loc is the position to insert; use -1 to append (typical OpenSSL pattern; exact behavior not documented here).

functions.name: TS_REQ_get_ext_d2i
functions.description: Parses and returns the decoded value of the extension identified by nid from the TS_REQ.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.
nid must be a valid extension NID.
crit and idx, if non-NULL, receive extension criticality and index information.
Returned pointer type depends on nid; caller is typically responsible for freeing it.

functions.name: TS_REQ_print_bio
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of a TS_REQ to a BIO.
requirements: bio must be a writable BIO.
a must be a valid TS_REQ pointer.

functions.name: TS_RESP_set_status_info
functions.description: Sets the status information on a TS_RESP.

info must be a valid TS_STATUS_INFO pointer; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_RESP_get_status_info
functions.description: Gets the TS_STATUS_INFO from a TS_RESP.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_RESP pointer.

functions.name: TS_RESP_set_tst_info
functions.description: Associates the signed token (PKCS7) and the TS_TST_INFO with a TS_RESP. Caller loses ownership of PKCS7 and TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_RESP pointer.
p7 must be a valid PKCS7 pointer; ownership is transferred to a.
tst_info must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer; ownership is transferred to a.

functions.name: TS_RESP_get_token
functions.description: Returns the PKCS7 token from a TS_RESP.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_RESP pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_RESP_get_tst_info
functions.description: Returns the TS_TST_INFO from a TS_RESP.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_RESP pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_version
functions.description: Sets the version on a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
version must be a valid TS protocol version integer (exact range unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_version
functions.description: Gets the version from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_policy_id
functions.description: Sets the policy OID for a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
policy_id must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_policy_id
functions.description: Gets the policy OID from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_msg_imprint
functions.description: Sets the message imprint in a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
msg_imprint must be a valid TS_MSG_IMPRINT; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_msg_imprint
functions.description: Gets the message imprint from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_serial
functions.description: Sets the serial number for a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
serial must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_serial
functions.description: Gets the serial number from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_time
functions.description: Sets the timestamp (GeneralizedTime) in a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
gtime must be a valid ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_time
functions.description: Gets the timestamp from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_accuracy
functions.description: Sets the accuracy structure for a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
accuracy must be a valid TS_ACCURACY; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_accuracy
functions.description: Gets the accuracy from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_set_seconds
functions.description: Sets the seconds component of accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
seconds must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_get_seconds
functions.description: Gets the seconds component from accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_set_millis
functions.description: Sets the milliseconds component of accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
millis must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_get_millis
functions.description: Gets the milliseconds component from accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_set_micros
functions.description: Sets the microseconds component of accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
micros must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_ACCURACY_get_micros
functions.description: Gets the microseconds component from accuracy.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_ACCURACY pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_ordering
functions.description: Sets the ordering flag in TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
ordering should be 0 or non-zero to clear/set.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ordering
functions.description: Gets the ordering flag from TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_nonce
functions.description: Sets the nonce for the TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
nonce must be a valid ASN1_INTEGER; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_nonce
functions.description: Gets the nonce from the TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_set_tsa
functions.description: Sets the TSA name (GENERAL_NAME) in TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
tsa must be a valid GENERAL_NAME; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_tsa
functions.description: Gets the TSA name from TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_exts
functions.description: Returns the extension stack from a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Returned stack is owned by a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_ext_free
functions.description: Frees the extensions contained in a TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
Only frees extensions within a; a itself remains valid.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_count
functions.description: Returns the number of extensions in TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_by_NID
functions.signature: int TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_by_NID(TS_TST_INFO *a, int nid, int lastpos);
functions.description: Finds an extension index by NID in the TS_TST_INFO, starting after lastpos.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
nid must be a valid extension NID.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_by_OBJ
functions.signature: int TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_by_OBJ(TS_TST_INFO *a, const ASN1_OBJECT *obj, int lastpos);
functions.description: Finds an extension index by object OID in the TS_TST_INFO, starting after lastpos.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
obj must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT pointer.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_by_critical
functions.description: Finds the next extension index in TS_TST_INFO matching the critical flag.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
crit should be 0 or 1.
lastpos controls search position; use -1 to start at beginning.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext
functions.description: Retrieves an extension at index loc from TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
loc must be a valid index.
Returned pointer is associated with a; do not free it independently.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_delete_ext
functions.description: Removes and returns the extension at index loc from TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
loc must be a valid index.
Caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned X509_EXTENSION.

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_add_ext
functions.description: Adds an X509 extension to the TS_TST_INFO at the specified position.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
ex must be a valid, dynamically allocated X509_EXTENSION; ownership is transferred to a on success.
loc is the position to insert; use -1 to append (exact behavior not documented here).

functions.name: TS_TST_INFO_get_ext_d2i
functions.description: Parses and returns the decoded value of the extension identified by nid from the TS_TST_INFO.
requirements: a must be a valid TS_TST_INFO pointer.
nid must be a valid extension NID.
crit and idx, if non-NULL, receive extension criticality and index information.
Returned pointer type depends on nid; caller is typically responsible for freeing it.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new TS_RESP_CTX for generating timestamp responses using the default library context.
requirements: Caller must free the returned context with TS_RESP_CTX_free.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_new_ex
functions.description: Allocates a new TS_RESP_CTX with an explicit OpenSSL library context and property query string.
requirements: libctx may be NULL to use the default library context.
propq may be NULL or a property query string to select implementations.
Caller must free the returned context with TS_RESP_CTX_free.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a TS_RESP_CTX and associated resources.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect).
After this call, ctx must not be used.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_signer_cert
functions.description: Sets the signer certificate used to sign timestamp responses. Required parameter.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
signer must be a valid X509 certificate.
This parameter must be set before generating a response.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_signer_key
functions.description: Sets the private key corresponding to the signer certificate. Required parameter.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
key must be a valid EVP_PKEY matching the signer certificate.
This parameter must be set before generating a response.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_signer_digest
functions.description: Sets the digest algorithm used for signing the timestamp token.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
signer_digest must be a valid EVP_MD; it is not copied (shared per comment in add_md; exact ownership here is unspecified/unknown).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_ess_cert_id_digest
functions.description: Sets the digest algorithm used in the ESSCertIDv2 attribute for identifying the signing certificate by digest.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
md must be a valid EVP_MD.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_def_policy
functions.description: Sets the default acceptable TSA policy OID. Required parameter for response generation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
def_policy must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT OID.
This parameter must be set before generating a response.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_certs
functions.description: Sets additional certificates to include in the response. By default, no additional certs are included.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
certs, if provided, must be a valid STACK_OF(X509); ownership semantics not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_add_policy
functions.description: Adds an acceptable TSA policy OID. By default, only the default policy is accepted.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
policy must be a valid ASN1_OBJECT OID.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_add_md
functions.description: Adds an acceptable message digest algorithm for requests. No digests are accepted by default.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
md must be a valid EVP_MD.
Per header comment, the md argument is shared with the caller (not copied).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_accuracy
functions.signature: int TS_RESP_CTX_set_accuracy(TS_RESP_CTX *ctx, int secs, int millis, int micros);
functions.description: Sets the accuracy fields (seconds, milliseconds, microseconds) to be included in responses. Accuracy is not included by default.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
secs, millis, micros should be non-negative integers (exact allowed ranges not specified).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_clock_precision_digits
functions.description: Sets the number of decimal digits of clock precision (0=seconds, 3=milliseconds, 6=microseconds). Default is 0.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
clock_precision_digits should be <= TS_MAX_CLOCK_PRECISION_DIGITS (6).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_add_flags
functions.description: Adds response generation flags (e.g., TS_TSA_NAME, TS_ORDERING, TS_ESS_CERT_ID_CHAIN).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
flags should be a bitwise OR of defined TS_* flag values.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_serial_cb
functions.description: Sets a callback to generate unique serial numbers (<160 bits) for responses. Default returns a constant.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
cb must follow TS_serial_cb signature and return a unique ASN1_INTEGER less than 160 bits; non-NULL recommended for production.
data is an opaque pointer passed to the callback.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_time_cb
functions.description: Sets a callback to supply the current time. Default uses gettimeofday()/gmtime().
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
cb must set sec and usec since Jan 1, 1970 and return non-zero on success; return 0 on failure.
data is an opaque pointer passed to the callback.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_extension_cb
functions.description: Sets a callback to process TS_TST_INFO extensions prior to signing. Default rejects all extensions.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
cb must return non-zero on success (processed) or 0 on error and set status/failure info.
data is an opaque pointer passed to the callback.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_status_info
functions.signature: int TS_RESP_CTX_set_status_info(TS_RESP_CTX *ctx, int status, const char *text);
functions.description: Sets the status and optional text in the response context (usable from callbacks).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
status should be a TS_STATUS_* value.
text may be NULL or a C-string; maximum acceptable length is unspecified here (TS_MAX_STATUS_LENGTH exists globally).

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_set_status_info_cond
functions.description: Sets status info only if the current context status is TS_STATUS_GRANTED.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
status should be a TS_STATUS_* value.
text may be NULL or a C-string.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_add_failure_info
functions.description: Adds a failure_info bit to the response context. Bits correspond to TS_INFO_* constants.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
failure should be one of the TS_INFO_* constants.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_get_request
functions.description: Returns the TS_REQ currently being processed by the response context (usable in callbacks).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the context; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_RESP_CTX_get_tst_info
functions.description: Returns the TS_TST_INFO being constructed (usable in callbacks).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_RESP_CTX pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the context; do not free it.

functions.name: TS_RESP_create_response
functions.description: Creates a signed response (TS_RESP) for the request read from req_bio using the given context. On errors, sets status info appropriately; returns NULL only for fatal allocation errors per comment.
requirements: ctx must be configured with required parameters (signer cert, signer key, default policy at minimum).
req_bio must be a readable BIO containing a DER-encoded TS_REQ.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned TS_RESP.

functions.name: TS_RESP_verify_signature
functions.description: Verifies the signer's certificate and the PKCS7 signature on a timestamp token using provided certs and store.
requirements: token must be a valid PKCS7 timestamp token.
certs may provide untrusted chain certificates (may be NULL).
store should be an initialized X509_STORE with trust anchors (may be NULL).
signer_out, if non-NULL, may receive the signer's certificate (ownership semantics not specified here; unknown).

functions.name: TS_RESP_verify_response
functions.description: Verifies a TS response according to the flags and parameters set in TS_VERIFY_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX with appropriate flags (e.g., TS_VFY_SIGNATURE typically required).
response must be a valid TS_RESP pointer.

functions.name: TS_RESP_verify_token
functions.description: Verifies a timestamp PKCS7 token using parameters in TS_VERIFY_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX with appropriate flags.
token must be a valid PKCS7 timestamp token.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new TS_VERIFY_CTX.
requirements: Caller must free the context with TS_VERIFY_CTX_free or TS_VERIFY_CTX_cleanup followed by free.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_init
functions.description: Initializes a TS_VERIFY_CTX structure in-place to default values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, allocated TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
After init, caller may customize fields; no return value.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a TS_VERIFY_CTX and associated resources.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect).
After this call, ctx must not be used.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up a TS_VERIFY_CTX without freeing the memory of the ctx itself.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
Use this when ctx was not allocated with TS_VERIFY_CTX_new.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_flags
functions.description: Sets verification flags (e.g., TS_VFY_SIGNATURE, TS_VFY_POLICY, TS_VFY_IMPRINT, etc.).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
f is a bitwise OR of TS_VFY_* flags.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_add_flags
functions.description: Adds verification flags to the existing set in the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
f is a bitwise OR of TS_VFY_* flags.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_data
functions.description: [Deprecated] Sets the BIO containing the data to be hashed and verified against the token (unclear semantics per deprecation note).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
b must be a readable BIO containing the data to timestamp/verify.
Deprecated in 3.4; prefer TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_data.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_data
functions.description: Sets the BIO containing the data to be hashed and verified; set0 implies the context takes ownership/reference without copying.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
b must be a readable BIO; its lifetime becomes tied to ctx (do not free b separately after setting).

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_imprint
functions.signature: unsigned char *TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_imprint(TS_VERIFY_CTX *ctx, unsigned char *hexstr, long len);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Sets the expected message imprint (hash) for verification (semantics unclear per deprecation note).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
hexstr must point to a buffer of length len; format/ownership semantics are unclear (deprecated).
Deprecated in 3.4; prefer TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_imprint.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_imprint
functions.signature: int TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_imprint(TS_VERIFY_CTX *ctx, unsigned char *hexstr, long len);
functions.description: Sets the expected message imprint (raw bytes) for verification; set0 implies the context takes ownership/reference without copying.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
hexstr must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; caller must not free hexstr after setting since ownership is transferred/tied to ctx.
len must be non-negative.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_store
functions.description: [Deprecated] Sets the X509_STORE used for certificate path validation (semantics unclear per deprecation note).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
s must be an initialized X509_STORE.
Deprecated in 3.4; prefer TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_store.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_store
functions.description: Sets the X509_STORE to be used for certificate validation; set0 implies the context holds the reference without copying.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
s must be an initialized X509_STORE; caller should not free s independently after setting.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set_certs
functions.description: [Deprecated] Sets a stack of untrusted certificates to assist path building (semantics unclear per deprecation note).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
certs must be a STACK_OF(X509).
Deprecated in 3.4; prefer TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_certs.

functions.name: TS_VERIFY_CTX_set0_certs
functions.description: Sets a stack of untrusted certificates; set0 implies the context takes ownership/reference without copying.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TS_VERIFY_CTX pointer.
certs must be a STACK_OF(X509); caller should not free it independently after setting.
